title: Technology Empowerment and Institutional Pressure: A Study of the Impact of Digital Transformation on Financial Statement Information Quality–From the Perspective of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Greenwashing Governance
summary: Against the background of the comprehensive green transformation of the economy and society, the relationship between digital transformation and corporate environmental disclosure has become increasingly prominent. Most existing studies focus on the effects of digital transformation on operating efficiency or environmental performance, but they have not answered whether digital transformation can improve environmental information quality and then transmit this improvement to the field of financial information. Using Chinese A-share listed companies from 2011 to 2021 as the research sample, this study empirically examines the effect of corporate digital transformation on financial statement information quality. The results show that digital transformation significantly inhibits ESG greenwashing, further reduces earnings management, and improves accounting information comparability. The mechanism analysis shows that digital transformation improves corporate information quality by strengthening internal control, alleviating financing constraints, and enhancing external supervision. The heterogeneity analysis shows that the governance effect of digital transformation is more significant in firms with greater information asymmetry and lower institutional ownership. The findings provide evidence for promoting high-quality corporate development and improving the information environment of the capital market.

title: Fintech Innovations and Accounting Practices
summary: Financial technology (FinTech) innovations are transforming traditional accounting practices by integrating automation, artificial intelligence, blockchain, cloud computing, robotic process automation, big data analytics, and digital payment systems into financial operations. This study examines the impact of FinTech innovations on accounting processes, financial reporting, auditing, internal control, managerial decision-making, and the evolving professional role of accountants. The research adopts a conceptual and descriptive methodology based on secondary data obtained from academic articles, professional reports, regulatory publications, and industry studies. Findings reveal that FinTech improves the speed, accuracy, transparency, reliability, and accessibility of accounting information while reducing manual errors, transaction costs, processing time, and repetitive work. Cloud-based accounting facilitates real-time recording, data synchronisation, collaboration, and remote access to financial information. Artificial intelligence supports fraud detection, risk assessment, predictive analysis, and financial decision-making. Blockchain technology enhances the security, reliability, transparency, and traceability of transactions, while automation simplifies bookkeeping, bank reconciliation, taxation, payroll, auditing, and regulatory compliance activities. Big data analytics also enable organisations to identify financial trends, evaluate performance, and make strategic decisions. However, FinTech adoption creates several challenges, including cybersecurity threats, data privacy concerns, system integration difficulties, regulatory uncertainty, high implementation and maintenance costs, resistance to technological change, and a shortage of accounting professionals with adequate technical skills. The study further highlights that accountants are gradually shifting from traditional record-keeping and transaction-processing to roles towards analytical, advisory, strategic, and technology-oriented responsibilities. Continuous professional development, digital literacy, ethical awareness, cybersecurity knowledge, and effective internal controls are therefore essential for successful FinTech adoption. The paper concludes that FinTech does not eliminate the need for accountants; instead, it strengthens their capabilities and reshapes accounting into a more efficient, data-driven, transparent, and decision-focused function. Organisations should adopt FinTech gradually while ensuring regulatory compliance, employee training, data security, responsible technology use, and strong governance and oversight mechanisms.

title: Digital Economy-Driven AI Innovation and Supply Chain Resilience: From Technological Capability to Risk-Buffering Capacity
summary: Frequent disruptions to global supply chains have made the conversion of AI innovation into firms’ capacity to withstand and respond to supply chain risks an important issue in the digital economy. Using 36,658 firm-year observations for Chinese listed companies from 2007 to 2025, this study examines the effect of AI innovation on supply chain resilience. The baseline specification includes firm-level controls, firm fixed effects, year fixed effects, and province-by-year fixed effects, while further analyses examine the role of cost stickiness and the moderating effects of the digital economy, the market-based allocation of data elements, and economic policy uncertainty. AI innovation has a significantly positive coefficient of 0.5084. This effect is concentrated among manufacturing firms and is stronger for state-owned and non-loss-making firms. AI innovation improves supply chain resilience by reducing cost stickiness; city-level digital economy development and the market-based allocation of data elements strengthen this effect, whereas economic policy uncertainty weakens it. By explaining how AI-related technological capability translates into supply chain risk-buffering capacity, this study provides evidence for firms seeking to deepen AI applications and for governments improving digital infrastructure, data trading institutions, and the policy environment.

title: Dual-discipline or governance decoupling? How corporate governance and ESG disclosure shape the earnings management-financial performance nexus in an emerging market
summary: Purpose This study examines the relationship between earnings management (EM) and financial performance (FP) in Vietnamese listed firms, while investigating the moderating roles of corporate governance (CG) and environmental, social and governance (ESG) disclosure within this nexus. Design/methodology/approach This study employs panel data from 303 non-financial listed firms over the period 2017–2024. A two-step System Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimator is applied to address endogeneity, simultaneity bias and dynamic persistence. Marginal effects are estimated to examine how EM affects FP across CG and ESG disclosure levels. Findings The findings show that the effect of EM on FP is contingent upon governance quality and ESG disclosure. When these mechanisms operate jointly, EM is more effectively constrained. Conversely, when ESG disclosure is high but governance quality is weak, the negative impact of EM becomes more pronounced, particularly for real EM. The findings are consistent with an expectation trap mechanism, whereby higher ESG disclosure may increase stakeholder expectations, while misalignment between disclosure and governance is associated with stronger negative market reactions. Overall, the evidence suggests that transparency alone is insufficient without credible internal governance. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by developing a dual-discipline mechanism that captures the interaction between internal governance and external transparency. By separating CG from ESG disclosure, it avoids measurement overlap and clarifies their distinct roles. Moreover, a hand-collected Corporate Governance Index (CGI), based on the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Principles of Corporate Governance (2015, 2023), provides a context-sensitive measure of governance quality in an emerging market.

title: Artificial intelligence and green supply chain management in Chinese listed firms
summary: Abstract As the core driving force of the new generation of industrial revolution, artificial intelligence technology has brought new opportunities for empowering enterprise green transformation and advancing sustainability. Focusing on Chinese A-share listed companies and based on unbalanced panel data from 2016 to 2024, this study systematically examines the impact, transmission mechanisms, and heterogeneity of AI applications on green supply chain management (GSCM). Drawing on the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities theory, this paper constructs an integrated theoretical framework that traces a causal link between AI applications through firm internal capabilities to green supply chain management. The empirical results show that AI applications significantly promote GSCM. Mechanism tests reveal that AI indirectly enhances GSCM by improving four dimensions of firm internal capabilities: green innovation, ESG performance, supply chain efficiency, and resource integration. In addition, heterogeneity analysis indicates that the enabling effect of AI on GSCM is more pronounced in state-owned enterprises, firms with higher environmental information disclosure quality, and firms in heavily polluting industries. This study deepens theoretical understanding of the relationship between AI and GSCM, reveals the micro-mechanisms and boundary conditions of AI-enabled GSCM, and provides practical insights for policymakers to guide firms in strategically applying AI and building efficient and collaborative green supply chains.

title: Corporate Greenwashing-Oriented Pseudo-Innovation: A Literature Review
summary: Against the backdrop of China's dual-carbon goals and the rapid expansion of ESG disclosure requirements, the volume of corporate green innovation has risen sharply. At the same time, more formalistic and strategic forms of innovation have appeared, often taking green patents and R&D expenditure as visible signs of environmental commitment. Drawing on both Chinese- and English-language studies, this review examines greenwashing-oriented pseudo-innovation from four perspectives: conceptual meaning, antecedents, economic consequences, and governance. Particular attention is paid to the boundary between this form of pseudo-innovation and conventional verbal greenwashing or broader forms of pseudo-corporate social responsibility. The review also summarizes theoretical developments and empirical evidence, identifies unresolved issues in conceptualization, identification and measurement, and governance, and outlines directions for future research. Existing studies suggest that greenwashing-oriented pseudo-innovation is an opportunistic strategy in which apparently substantive innovative actions are used as a symbolic vehicle to obtain legitimacy-related benefits. Such behavior can weaken market trust, damage corporate reputation, and distort the allocation of resources intended for genuine green innovation. Further work is therefore needed to sharpen the concept, improve measurement, and develop more targeted governance mechanisms.

title: FINANCIAL INCLUSION, DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND ENERGY CONSUMPTION DYNAMICS: EVIDENCE FROM OIC ECONOMIES
summary: This study examines the impact of digitalization and financial inclusion on energy consumption across 40 OIC member countries from 2001 to 2022. The research used several advanced panel econometric techniques, including cross-sectional dependence and slope heterogeneity tests, CIPS, IPS, and LLC unit root tests, Pedroni, Kao, and Westerlund cointegration tests, FMOLS and DOLS long-run estimators and the Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MMQR) approach. The findings indicate that digitalization and financial inclusion significantly reduce energy consumption in overall OIC countries and particularly in higher-income OIC countries by improving energy efficiency, facilitating technological innovation, and promoting the adoption of energy-efficient technologies. However, in lower-income OIC countries, digitalization and financial inclusion increase energy consumption due to increasing industrial activity, growing access to energy-dependent technologies, and rising economic participation. Furthermore, industrialization and population are found to increase energy consumption across all country groups. The interaction effect between Digitalization and financial inclusion indicates that their combined role contributes to energy sustainability, especially in higher-income OIC countries. The study highlights important policy implications for sustainable energy management in OIC economies. Policymakers should promote digital infrastructure, expand inclusive financial systems, and encourage green financing mechanisms to accelerate the adoption of energy-efficient technologies while ensuring sustainable energy transition pathways, particularly in lower-income OIC countries.

title: Financial mechanisms for implementing green projects in the mining industry
summary: This study examines financial mechanisms for implementing green projects in the mining industry as a tool for environmentally responsible modernization, improvement of the energy efficiency and reduction of environmental risks. It is justified that high resource and energy intensity, waste generation, land disturbance, water consumption and emissions of pollutants require a transition from a compensation-based environmental protection approach to project financing of environmental transformation. The key tools identified include the green bonds, ESG loans, subsidies, public-private partnership, climate finance and targeted investments in land reclamation, water treatment, waste recycling and energy-efficient equipment. The article proposes an organizational and economic approach to assessing green projects with account of environmental effects, life-cycle costs, investment risks and their impact on sustainability of mining companies.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Accounting: Applications, Benefits, Challenges and Future Prospects
summary: The swift advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing conventional accounting practices by facilitating enhanced automation, precision, efficiency, and data-informed decision-making. AI tools are progressively utilized in various fields such as bookkeeping, financial reporting, auditing, fraud detection, tax management, financial analysis, and forecasting. It is crucial for accounting professionals, organizations, educators, and students to comprehend these applications as the accounting field continues to evolve with technological progress. Even though previous research has looked at the potential of AI in accounting, more knowledge is still needed about how AI is being used in various accounting activities, the advantages it offers, and the obstacles to its adoption. More research is needed on issues pertaining to data protection, cybersecurity, implementation costs, ethical concerns, transparency, and the evolving skills needed for accounting professionals. This study's primary goal is to investigate the use of artificial intelligence in accounting and to evaluate its main advantages, difficulties, and potential. Based on secondary data gathered from scholarly publications, professional reports, research papers, and other pertinent sources, the study uses a descriptive research methodology. The results show that AI may enhance financial decision-making, decrease tedious human labour, increase fraud detection, and speed and improve accounting procedures. However, the right technology infrastructure, qualified personnel, moral principles, and efficient data governance are necessary for successful deployment. According to the study, AI should be seen as a supplement to accounting professionals rather than a replacement for them. To prepare professionals for the future of accounting, accounting companies and educational institutions should concentrate on building technical, analytical, and ethical abilities relevant to AI.

title: When does ESG create value? Corporate governance as a moderating mechanism in Indian firms
summary: This study examines whether corporate governance determines if environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance translates into financial value for Indian listed firms. It draws on 711 firm year observations for 341 firms listed on the National Stock Exchange of India between 2019 and 2023. ESG data come from Refinitiv and accounting data from CMIE Prowess. The analysis uses firm and year fixed effects regressions with standard errors clustered at the firm level. Financial performance is measured by return on assets (ROA), with Tobin’s Q used as a market-based robustness check. Governance quality is captured by a composite index covering board size, board independence, board gender diversity, CEO duality, audit committee independence, and foreign institutional ownership. ESG performance has no statistically significant direct association with either performance measure. However, the ESG–governance interaction is positive and significant for ROA, but insignificant for Tobin’s Q. At the pillar level, the social interaction is positive and significant for ROA, while the governance interaction is marginally significant and the environmental interaction is insignificant. Although the estimated ESG effect on ROA varies across governance levels, the conditional effects are individually insignificant. The findings highlight the importance of considering ESG performance and corporate governance jointly when evaluating firm performance, while cautioning against assuming automatic financial returns.

title: Factors Influencing Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Accounting for Sustainable Development: Evidence from Vietnamese Enterprises
summary: This study examines the factors influencing the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in accounting and evaluates its impact on the sustainable development of Vietnamese enterprises. The research model is developed by integrating three theoretical frameworks: the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework, the Resource-Based View (RBV), and the Diffusion of Innovation (DOI) theory. Data were collected from 362 valid questionnaires and analyzed using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) approach with SmartPLS 4 software. The findings indicate that technological readiness, top management support, human competency, and perceived benefits all have significant positive effects on AI adoption in accounting. Furthermore, AI adoption in accounting positively influences the sustainable development of enterprises. This study contributes empirical evidence on the determinants of AI adoption in accounting in the Vietnamese context and provides practical managerial implications for promoting digital transformation and achieving sustainable business development.

title: Emerging technologies, organizational change, and financial innovation: A multi-country study from the Arab region
summary: This study evaluates digital transformation in the Arab region, examining how advanced financial technologies, driven by COVID-19 and global conflicts, impact business organizational structures, adoption challenges, and economic performance. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, primary data were gathered via simple random sampling from 2,168 investors, fintech users, and financial professionals across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Bahrain, Qatar, Jordan, and Morocco. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression and other statistical methods. Results reveal varied adoption rates across countries. AI, blockchain, and big data analytics significantly enhanced efficiency, decision-making quality, and customer service innovation. Bank-fintech partnerships enabled digital transformation, while neobanks and mobile payment systems intensified market competition, driving businesses toward more agile, customer-centric strategies. The insights offer policymakers and regulatory authorities actionable guidance to strengthen digital infrastructure, governance, and institutional flexibility across the region. Offering evidence from multiple countries, this study adds to the literature on financial innovation and organizational change in emerging Arab economies during more uncertain times.

title: Nonlinear effects of digital transformation on the geographical distribution of supply chain partners
summary: Using a sample of Chinese listed firms from 2010 to 2024, this study finds an inverted U-shaped relationship between digital transformation and supply chain distance. That is, distance initially expands as digitalization increases but contracts at advanced levels of digitalization. The mechanism analysis reveals that risk perception is a common channel affecting both supplier and customer distance, whereas business concentration operates primarily on the supplier side. Further analysis shows that digital transformation has a U-shaped effect on geographical concentration and an inverted U-shaped effect on coverage breadth.

title: Mutual Fund Ownership and ESG Rating Divergence
summary: This study demonstrates that mutual fund ownership significantly reduces corporate ESG rating divergence in the context of Chinese listed firms. The effect is more pronounced in firms with higher financial reporting opacity, more severe agency costs, and greater operating performance risk. The evidence further shows that mutual funds alleviate ESG rating divergence by improving corporate ESG information disclosure and increasing analyst coverage. These findings offer novel insights and practical strategies for alleviating ESG rating divergence in capital markets.

title: Financial Literacy and Green Finance: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: Investments in green projects have become important in the present era due to environmental concerns and the need for sustainable development has arisen. However, the participation of individuals is limited when green projects or green investing is concerned. Financial literacy is one of the reasons which may influence investment in green projects as individuals with financial awareness and financial knowledge are able to make informed investment decisions. It may also depend on individual’s willingness and understanding to invest in green projects. This study will be focusing on examining the relationship between financial literacy and green finance and what factors are held responsible for boosting green investment decision making among individuals. A systematic literature review approach is adopted by examining existing literature from 2010 to 2026 which focuses on sustainable financial literacy, green finance, financial literacy and the factors affecting green investment decision making such as policies awareness, government policies effectiveness, financial awareness programs, environmental awareness and many more. Based upon the literature review, it concludes that financial literacy has strong relationship with green finance but financial literacy is not the only factor which influences green finance there are various other factors which influences investments in green projects like policy awareness, government subsidies, digital financial literacy, sustainable financial literacy, environment awareness, policies effectiveness and fintech adoption. This study also suggests the policymakers to make effective policies which makes active participation in green projects. Secondly, financial education programs should be implemented for adults as well as financial literacy must be taught as a subject to every child through formal mode of education. Thus, this study helps in understanding the factors which influence the relationship between financial literacy and green finance identifies the areas for future research.

title: Criteria and indicators of corporate social responsibility of enterprises in wartime conditions
summary: The article examines the criteria and indicators of corporate social responsibility under the specific conditions of wartime business operations. The study aims to substantiate and systematize criteria and indicators that can comprehensively characterize responsible corporate behavior and reflect changes in the needs and expectations of key stakeholder groups under war-related challenges. The study’s methodological framework draws on analysis and synthesis, systematization and generalization of scientific approaches, the stakeholder approach, and comparative analysis of contemporary research on corporate social responsibility in stable and crisis conditions. The study systematizes six interrelated criteria of corporate social responsibility: social and labor responsibility, economic responsibility, responsibility toward consumers and business partners, ethical and managerial responsibility, environmental responsibility, and social responsibility toward communities and society. The main indicators characterizing each area of responsible corporate behavior are identified. The wartime dimension should not be treated as an isolated area of corporate social responsibility. Instead, it should be considered as a cross-cutting characteristic that changes the content and priority of individual indicators within the established criteria. Wartime-specific manifestations include preserving employment, supporting mobilized employees and their families, ensuring business continuity, adapting business processes to war-related risks, providing humanitarian assistance, supporting local communities, assisting affected populations, and participating in recovery processes. The study’s scientific novelty lies in systematizing CSR criteria by combining universal characteristics of responsible corporate behavior with specific indicators shaped by the wartime environment. Unlike approaches focused primarily on individual social initiatives or general CSR dimensions, the proposed system emphasizes the need to reflect changes in the practical content and priorities of corporate responsibility under extraordinary external conditions. The practical significance of the results depends on the ability to use the proposed system as a basis for further assessment of the level of corporate social responsibility, identification of problematic components, and development of appropriate managerial measures. The proposed approach can also support the development of internal corporate monitoring systems and the selection of relevant indicators according to the characteristics of a particular enterprise, industry, region, and level of war-related risks. Further research should focus on developing a methodological approach to assessing the level of corporate social responsibility and adapting the proposed indicators to sectoral and regional characteristics of business operation during wartime. title: Institutional and organizational framework for implementing strategic priorities of the development of Ukraine’s logistics information and telecommunication system
summary: The article substantiates the theoretical, legal, and managerial foundations for establishing an institutional environment to support the implementation of strategic priorities for developing Ukraine’s Logistics Information and Telecommunication System (LITS) under conditions of martial law and post-war economic recovery. The study conceptualizes the multi-level institutional architecture of LITS as a coherent system integrating national, interdepartmental, regional, sector-specific, and corporate governance tiers. The methodological framework includes institutional analysis, systematic structural synthesis, evolutionary modeling, and scenario management. The analysis shows that implementing LITS target parameters requires clear distribution of authority among market participants, aligned inter-agency interaction protocols, multi-channel investment allocation, and robust cybersecurity protocols. The paper systematizes Ukraine’s regulatory foundation, including national economic, regional, and transport strategies, as well as legal acts governing multimodal transport, electronic documentation, and cybersecurity. International best practices (EU, USA, Japan, South Korea, China) in managing logistics digitalization are analyzed. The study highlights the relevance of adapting the European Union’s eFTI regulation, TEN-T corridor management, and digital single-window frameworks to guarantee seamless interoperability with EU transport networks. The author develops a multi-tiered institutional model centered around a unified decentralized logistics data contour. This model connects public-private partnerships, national registries, and analytical platforms with iterative feedback loops for continuous monitoring, risk assessment, and scenario adjustment. title: Current strategies for financing enterprise development: an innovative and harmonious approach
summary: This article examines corporate financial development through innovative and harmonious approaches. The main trend in the development of corporate financial structures is the use of financial technologies that accelerate investment attraction and increase the transparency of financial transactions. This paper examines one of the latest tools for the financial sector’s digital transformation: the tokenization of real assets. This mechanism provides access to new investment opportunities, allowing enterprises to transfer their assets into the digital realm and trade them on relevant markets to attract additional funding. The paper also examines ESG financing, which integrates environmental, social, and governance criteria into investment and financial decision-making. The paper establishes that implementing ESG principles enables companies to attract financial resources through specialized sustainable financing mechanisms, namely green bonds, social bonds, sustainable development bonds, ESG loans, and investments by specialized ESG funds. This paper examines the trend toward the digital transformation of financial management, which involves implementing artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies to streamline business processes and improve analytical capabilities and decision-making efficiency. The paper examines crowdfunding and venture capital as innovative mechanisms for raising funds from investors via specialized online platforms at various stages of a company’s development. Innovative opportunities for the financial and harmonious development of enterprises hold significant potential for further advancement through digitalization—specifically by leveraging cutting-edge platforms to attract investment, manage accounting, and monitor processes. title: Corporate governance and green innovation performance: a TCCM-based systematic literature review
summary: This study reviews and synthesizes literature linking corporate governance mechanisms to green innovation performance. It examines how board structure, ownership patterns, executive incentives, and ESG practices shape firms' pursuit of sustainability-driven innovation across institutional contexts. Using the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis) protocol and TCCM (Theory-Context-Characteristics-Methodology) framework, the review analyses 213 articles published between 2015 and 2025. Bibliometric mapping and content analysis identify foundations, methodological trends, and differences in the governance-innovation nexus. Findings show that board diversity, independence, and environmental competence improve green innovation performance by supporting perspectives and stakeholder responsiveness. Ownership structure, CEO duality, and ESG disclosure influence innovation outcomes, with effects varying by institutional quality and industry context. Quantitative and single-theory approaches dominate, highlighting the need for integrated frameworks and methods. The study positions governance as both a compliance mechanism and a driver of competitiveness and value creation, providing a synthesis and a research agenda for sustainability-focused corporate governance.

title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE QUALITY AND EXTERNAL AUDIT QUALITY ON EARNINGS MANAGEMENT IN NIGERIA’S OIL AND GAS SECTOR: A POST-COVID-19 PERIOD
summary: This study investigates the impact of corporate governance quality and external audit quality on earnings management in Nigeria‘s oil and gas sector during the post-COVID- 19 period. Drawing from 56 firm-year observations of seven listed companies between the periods 2018-2025, the study explores both discretionary accruals and real earnings management (REM) as key proxies for earnings manipulation. Using ordinary least square panel regression models, the findings reveal a significant increase in earnings management practices following the COVID-19 pandemic, indicating heightened managerial incentives to manage earnings under economic pressure. It recommends stronger regulatory oversight, enhanced board structures, and improved audit practices to safeguard financial reporting integrity. The findings offer valuable insights for policymakers, regulators, and stakeholders seeking to strengthen institutional responses to future economic shocks. title: From digital to green: the effect of corporate digital transformation on pollution emission intensity
summary: Digital transformation is a key driver of the optimization and upgrading of China’s economic structure and a core element in the transition of China’s economic and social development towards green growth. This paper empirically analyzes the impact of corporate digital transformation on pollution emission intensity and its mechanisms. The results indicate that digital transformation significantly enhances corporate pollution emission intensity. The effect is more significant for enterprises in labor-intensive enterprises, and heavily polluting enterprises. Management efficiency, green technological innovation, and total factor productivity are important mechanisms through which digital transformation improves pollution emission intensity. This study provides empirical evidence and policy references for China to explore new paths for green and transformative development.

title: Influence of Quantification of Medical Supplies in Sustainability of Medical Supply Chain in Tanzania
summary: Services, product or supply chain is of utmost importance to any company. This study examining the influence of quantification of medical supplies in the sustainability of medical supply chain in Tanzania. The study utilized a quantitative approach that was paired with a cross-sectional survey research design, the study used a sample size of 150 respondents which included MSD personnel and staff from three medical health facilities. Data gathered from the respondents was analyzed by using multivariate regression analysis and the Statistical Package for Social Science version 32.0 (SPSS) was used to establish the correlation between supply chain factors and the sustainability of MSD’s medical supply chain. The findings revealed that the presence of a substantial relationship between the quantification and the sustainability of MSD’s medical supply chain since the P-values of the four variables drawn from multiple regression analyses were less than 0.05 so P-Values are 0.045 for quantification, while beta are 0.32811. The study concludes that sustainability with quantification, has proved important in the improvement of the entire value chain of medical supply at MSD, helping this institution address previous challenges related to frequent stockouts in healthcare facilities, promote Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), and guarantee the sustainable access and availability of pharmaceutical supplies in health facilities in a cost-effective way. From the key findings of the study, the researcher recommends policymakers should establish clear guidelines and regulations that incentivize and mandate sustainable practices within medical supply chains, managerial inefficiencies should be reduced through effectively engaging with its suppliers in order to identify areas of improvement as well as supplement supply with self-production of some essential medicines. title: Does environmental judicial reform influence audit fees? Evidence from China's environmental public interest litigation
summary: Purpose A careful study of the impact of the environmental public interest litigation (EPIL) pilot policy on audit fees would not only make the economic costs of judicial innovation in environmental governance but also the study would make a strong empirical statement about improving the environmental practices of the business community and audit policies. Design/methodology/approach We are working with a quasi-natural experiment in China based on its EPIL pilot program and we apply a difference-in-differences framework. Findings We find that firms in pilot regions pay 4.7% higher audit fees than non-pilot peers, a result robust to parallel-trend checks, placebo tests, propensity score matching and controls for concurrent policies. Mechanism evidence indicates that the EPIL pilot policy elevates auditors' perceived litigation and regulatory risk, leading to higher risk premia in pricing without commensurate increases in engagement hours. Effects are stronger for firms with weaker ESG, greater information asymmetry, higher auditor specialization, lower auditor workload pressure, or strong regional environmental policy enforcement. Further analysis shows that the increase in audit fees associated with the EPIL pilot policy does not lead to an improvement in audit quality. Originality/value (1) Incorporating bottom-up judicial environmental regulation (EPIL) into audit pricing frameworks, filling a research gap, (2) developing a unified auditor-auditee strategic interaction framework that reveals how external policies affect audit fee equilibrium through risk-sharing and resource allocation and (3) systematically explicating the transmission mechanism from environmental legal risks to audit risk premiums, enriching audit pricing theory.

title: The Impact of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Performance on Corporate Return on Investment: Evidence from China
summary: Improving corporate return on investment and generating returns for shareholders are among the important operating objectives of listed companies. With the development of the stakeholder concept, corporate operations have paid greater attention to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance; however, whether ESG performance can improve return on investment remains to be studied. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2009 to 2023, this study constructs a two-way fixed-effects model to examine the relationship between corporate ESG performance and return on investment. The empirical results show that ESG performance can significantly improve corporate return on investment, and this result remains valid after a series of robustness tests. The heterogeneity analysis finds that the positive effect of corporate ESG performance on corporate return on investment is more significant among non-state-owned enterprises, large firms, and young firms. The mechanism tests show that ESG performance can improve corporate return on investment by increasing total factor productivity and promoting corporate green innovation. This study provides empirical evidence from Chinese listed companies for understanding the economic consequences of ESG performance and also provides a reference for firms seeking to improve operating performance.

title: Enabling or weakening? Artificial intelligence and ambidextrous green innovation
summary: Purpose This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) adoption shapes firms' ambidextrous green innovation by inducing differential effects on exploratory and exploitative activities from an attention-based perspective. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the attention-based view, we theorize that AI adoption reconfigures organizational attention and technological capabilities, leading to divergent effects on green innovation. Using panel data from Chinese listed firms, we employ regression analyses to test these arguments. Findings AI adoption exerts a double-edged effect on ambidextrous green innovation. It significantly promotes exploratory green innovation by redirecting managerial attention toward forward-looking strategic issues, while suppressing exploitative green innovation by institutionalizing routine processes and reducing sustained attention to incremental improvements. Furthermore, Confucian cultural embeddedness, negative media coverage and institutional ownership strengthen the positive effect of AI on exploratory green innovation and mitigate its negative effect on exploitative green innovation. Practical implications These findings suggest that managers should align AI adoption with balanced attention allocation to avoid overemphasizing exploratory innovation at the expense of incremental improvements. Originality/value This study advances the literature by conceptualizing AI as an attention-restructuring mechanism that systematically differentiates firms' exploratory and exploitative green innovation. It contributes to research on AI and organizational ambidexterity by uncovering the contingent role of institutional and social contexts.

title: Carbon Emission Disclosure, Environmental Disclosure, Capital Intensity, and Corporate Financial Performance in Indonesia
summary: Purpose: This study analyzes the effect of carbon emission disclosure, environmental disclosure, and capital intensity on the financial performance of energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024.Research Methodology: This quantitative study uses the annual and sustainability reports of 38 companies selected through purposive sampling, yielding 190 firm-year observations. Carbon emission disclosure and environmental disclosure are measured with 18-item and 31-item indices, capital intensity with fixed assets to total assets, and financial performance with an adjusted return on assets series. The Random Effect Model is selected through the Chow, Hausman, and Lagrange Multiplier tests in EViews 12.Results: Carbon emission disclosure (B = 1.825225; p < 0.001) and environmental disclosure (B = 1.297164; p < 0.001) are positively and significantly associated with financial performance, whereas capital intensity is not significant (B = 0.027686; p = 0.8971). The three variables are simultaneously significant (F = 65.21017; p < 0.001), with an adjusted R² of 0.504757.Conclusions: Transparent carbon and environmental reporting is associated with stronger financial performance, whereas the proportion of fixed assets alone does not differentiate performance among energy companies.Limitations: The study covers one sector over five years, measures disclosure breadth rather than quality, and relies on an adjusted performance series that cannot be fully reproduced.Contributions: This study integrates stakeholder value-creation, legitimacy, signaling, and agency theories by demonstrating how carbon and environmental reporting jointly signal financial performance, providing insights for Indonesian firms, investors, and regulators.

title: How carbon border adjustment mechanism awareness shapes export strategic responses in Vietnam’s high carbon-emitting industries
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine the associations between Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) awareness, perceived compliance costs, green supply chain management, green innovation, export competitiveness and export performance among Vietnamese exporters. It also assesses whether measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) capability and government support condition selected relationships. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 227 firms in CBAM-exposed, carbon-intensive industries were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Robustness tests added firm-level controls, and multi-group analysis compared small, medium-sized and large firms after measurement invariance assessment. Findings CBAM awareness is positively associated with perceived compliance costs, green supply chain management and green innovation. Green innovation has the strongest positive association with export competitiveness, whereas perceived compliance costs are negatively associated with competitiveness. The aggregate green supply chain management–competitiveness relationship is non-significant but masks a negative coefficient for small firms, a positive coefficient for medium-sized firms and a negligible coefficient for large firms. Export competitiveness is positively associated with export performance. Originality/value Rather than proposing a general theory of CBAM, the paper contributes a firm-level, CBAM-specific dual-pathway model in Vietnam. It shows how an institutional awareness construct is associated concurrently with a compliance-cost pathway and an innovation pathway, while firm-size heterogeneity qualifies the aggregate evidence.

title: How Does Green Transformation Shapes Corporate Investment: The Conditional Role of Green Finance
summary: Drawing on firm-level observations from China’s A-share market over the 2008–2023 period, we examine whether and how corporate green transformation shapes firms’ inefficient investment. The results show that corporate green transformation significantly increases firms’ inefficient investment. Further evidence suggests that the increase in inefficient investment associated with green transformation is largely attributable to greater corporate over-investment. Specifically, corporate green transformation exacerbates inefficient investment by alleviating firms’ financing constraints and fostering green investment bubbles. The strength of this relationship is also closely associated with the development of green finance. In addition, we find significant heterogeneity in this effect across regions, industries, and firms.

title: From comparability to sustainability: new evidence on ESG performance and financial constraints
summary: We investigate how accounting comparability enhances corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and whether financial constraints mediate this relationship in China. Using a balanced panel of 786 non-financial A-share firms from 2010 to 2023, we employ panel-corrected standard errors (PCSE), the Sobel mediation test, and dynamic GMM estimations to address endogeneity concerns. We find that higher accounting comparability significantly enhances ESG performance, with the strongest effect observed in the governance pillar. Further analysis shows that accounting comparability reduces firms’ financial constraints by alleviating information asymmetry, whereas financial constraints adversely affect ESG performance. Mediation analyses confirm that financial constraints partially mediate the relationship between accounting comparability and ESG performance. The results are robust to alternative measures and model specifications. We suggest that enhancing accounting comparability can promote corporate sustainability by improving reporting quality and the financing environment, providing implications for policymakers, investors, and corporate managers.

title: Digital Economy and Four-Chain Coupling Synergy in Applied Higher Education Institutions: Effects and Mechanisms
summary: Digital transformation reshapes applied higher education institutions’ industrial demand perception, talent training, research commercialization and regional innovation participation. This paper constructs a complex-network evolutionary game model to explore the effects of the digital economy on four-chain coupling synergy among education, talent, innovation, and industry. Regional stakeholders are modeled as boundedly rational agents in heterogeneous collaborative networks, choosing between deep four-chain coupling and fragmented adaptation based on local payoffs. The payoff system includes digital benefit amplification, cost reduction, policy incentives, mismatch losses, spillover gains and governance quality. Analytical derivations show that digitalization increases the relative payoff of coupling and lowers the local collaboration threshold, with this effect reinforced by policy incentives and favorable network structures. Numerical analyses show that digital readiness, policy support, and governance quality promote high-coupling equilibria, while network topology shapes diffusion speed and stability; high coupling costs and low initial adoption hinder diffusion. Hub-oriented scale-free and core-periphery networks can accelerate strategy diffusion, whereas small-world networks converge more steadily but more slowly. This paper clarifies the micro-level cross-chain incentive mechanism of digitalization and identifies network conditions for universities to translate digital resources into regional innovation capacity, offering implications for higher education governance and regional digital policy.

title: How Does Green Industrial Policy Drive Sustained Green Innovation in Manufacturing Firms?
summary: Drawing on China’s Green Factory initiative and data from Chinese A-share listed manufacturing firms in the Shanghai and Shenzhen from 2012 to 2024, this study employs a staggered difference-in-differences model to examine the effect of green industrial policy on firms’ persistent green innovation. The results show that green industrial policy significantly promotes sustained green innovation. Mechanism analyses indicate that green industrial policy significantly promotes both knowledge recombination creation and knowledge recombination reuse, and both types of knowledge recombination are significantly positively associated with firms’ persistent green innovation. Heterogeneity analyses show that the effect is more pronounced in regions with stricter environmental regulation, firms with lower levels of green innovation bubbles, and firms with broader innovation boundaries, while it is weaker under less stringent regulation, more severe innovation bubbles, or narrower innovation boundaries. These findings provide empirical evidence and policy implications for jointly advancing economic development and environmental protection.

title: PROSPECTS FOR THE APPLICATION OF DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES IN THE ACCOUNTING AND AUDITING SYSTEM
summary: Purpose of the research – The purpose of this study is to examine the application areas of modern digital technologies in the accounting and auditing system, evaluate their impact on financial reporting, audit quality, and managerial efficiency, identify the existing challenges, and develop scientifically grounded recommendations regarding future development prospects. Research methodology – The study is based on a systematic approach and employs comparative analysis, content analysis, induction, and deduction methods. Contemporary scientific literature, international accounting and auditing standards, and studies on digital technologies were analyzed. Practical implications of the research – The findings of this study provide practical guidance for the digital transformation of accounting and auditing systems, the automation of audit procedures, the improvement of financial reporting quality, and the enhancement of managerial decision-making processes within organizations. Research findings – The study demonstrates that artificial intelligence, blockchain, Big Data, cloud computing, and robotic process automation (RPA) significantly improve the efficiency of accounting and auditing systems. Originality and scientific novelty – The study provides a comprehensive evaluation of the application of digital technologies in accounting and auditing by systematically analyzing the influence of various digital solutions on financial management 2 and audit quality. It presents scientifically grounded conclusions regarding the benefits, challenges, and future prospects of digital transformation and offers practical recommendations for the effective implementation of innovative technologies in accounting and auditing systems.

title: A text-mining analysis of climate risk disclosure and corporate energy efficiency in Chinese listed firms
summary: This study examines the association between climate risk disclosure and corporate energy efficiency using Chinese A-share data from 2012 to 2024. A firm-level disclosure index is constructed via text mining based on the TCFD framework. Two-way fixed effects models show a positive association, with a one-standard-deviation increase in disclosure corresponding to approximately a 3.6% increase in energy efficiency, robust to endogeneity tests. Transition risk disclosure has a stronger association with energy efficiency than physical risk; the difference widens further when standardized by each dimension’s dispersion. Mediation analysis indicates green innovation and eased financing constraints are partial channels whose separately estimated indirect effects sum to approximately 20% of the total effect, though the direct effect dominates. Heterogeneity analysis reveals stronger effects in state-owned, heavily polluting, and carbon pilot region firms, with insignificant effects outside pilot regions; the association also strengthens significantly after the launch of the national carbon market in 2021. The study contributes to the literature by shifting the focus from capital market reactions to real operational outcomes, distinguishing between physical and transition risk disclosure, and highlighting the role of institutional context in determining whether climate disclosure produces substantive effects on energy performance.

title: Legal Liability for Voluntary Disclosure and Management Forecast Accuracy: Quasi-Experimental Evidence from China’s Revised Securities Law
summary: Against the global debate over mandatory versus voluntary corporate disclosure, this study investigates whether strengthened legal accountability can sustain credible voluntary forward-looking information in emerging markets. Exploiting China’s Revised Securities Law (effective March 2020) as a quasi-natural experiment, which granted formal legal status to voluntary disclosure while substantially raising litigation risks for misleading statements, this paper examines the reform’s effect on management earnings-forecast accuracy. Given uniform nationwide implementation, I adopt an exposure-based difference-in-differences design using pre-reform firm-level voluntary forecasting intensity. Based on Chinese A-share listed firms over 2011–2023, I find that firms with higher pre-reform voluntary forecasting intensity exhibit significantly smaller forecast errors after the reform. The improvement is accompanied by less earnings management used to meet forecast targets and by higher-quality communication on stock-exchange investor platforms, consistent with two channels. The gains are concentrated in optimistic forecasts, with larger point estimates among firms with severe agency frictions. Stricter legal liability can thus sustain the credibility of the voluntary forecasts that firms choose to issue, with investor-firm communication infrastructure playing a complementary role.

title: FINTECH AS A DRIVER OF TRANSFORMATION IN THE FINANCIAL SECTOR
summary: This article examines FinTech as a factor in the transformation of the modern financial sector. It identifies and systematises the main areas in which financial technologies are influencing payment, banking, credit, investment and insurance services, risk management, regulatory and supervisory processes, and financial inclusion. It analyses current trends in the development of digital payments in Ukraine, in particular the dynamics of cashless transactions using payment cards, the development of instant credit transfers and the formation of the regulatory and technological environment for Open Banking. It explores the potential for using Big Data, machine learning and artificial intelligence in lending, insurance, asset management and risk management. The dynamics of global FinTech investments in 2024-2025 are analysed, and it is established that the growth in their total volume was accompanied by a reduction in the number of deals and an increase in the average capital per FinTech deal. It has been established that key manifestations of the FinTech transformation of Ukraine’s financial sector include the dominance of cashless transactions using payment cards, the development of instant payments and the introduction of open banking. It is demonstrated that the further spread of FinTech solutions creates the conditions for improving the accessibility of financial services, fostering competition and expanding financial inclusion. It has been determined that, alongside improvements in the technological efficiency, accessibility and personalisation of financial services, further FinTech transformation places greater demands on cybersecurity, personal data protection, operational resilience, the oversight of algorithmic models and consumer protection. The paper justifies the need to combine the introduction of financial innovations with ensuring financial stability, competitiveness and the proper management of digital risks in the process of the further transformation of Ukraine’s financial sector.

title: From digital villages to cleaner skies: how rural digitalization transforms environmental governance in China
summary: Rural environmental governance remains a persistent weak link in the regulatory systems of developing countries, where state capacity is constrained and pollution sources are dispersed. This study examines whether rural digitalization can mitigate this regulatory deficit and thereby reduce air pollution across Chinese villages. Drawing on panel data covering more than 300,000 administrative villages and an instrumental variable strategy, we find that a one-standard-deviation increase in digital village development lowers PM2.5 concentrations by 3.76 percent. Three reinforcing mechanisms drive this effect: digital finance relaxes the capital constraints that impede clean energy adoption; digital agriculture curbs fertilizer overuse through precision farming platforms; and digital governance strengthens environmental monitoring and enforcement in historically under-regulated jurisdictions. Monetizing the resulting reduction in mortality risk within a value-of-statistical-life framework, we estimate that the associated health benefits for China’s rural population amount to USD 18.6–64.6 billion. These findings reframe rural digitalization as a multi-channel governance instrument rather than merely a development tool, and they underscore the need for policymakers to incorporate environmental externalities into cost–benefit evaluations of digital infrastructure investment.

title: Unveiling the role of artificial intelligence in sustainable innovation: governance dynamics, dilemmas, and emerging insights
summary: Purpose This paper aims to examine how artificial intelligence contributes to green innovation, addressing conflicting evidence about its benefits and risks. It highlights the organizational and governance conditions that shape the effectiveness of artificial intelligence in supporting sustainable innovation. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis are used. The review organizes prior studies into three domains: robotics and automation, data handling and general artificial intelligence applications, while considering both supportive and critical perspectives. Bibliometric mapping identifies intellectual structures, thematic clusters, collaboration patterns and research gaps. A comprehensive artificial intelligence keyword framework ensures broad coverage and minimizes omissions. Findings The results indicate that artificial intelligence’s impact on green innovation depends strongly on organizational and contextual factors, including governance structures. Robotics and automation, data handling and general artificial intelligence applications each contribute differently to sustainability outcomes. The bibliometric analysis highlights central research networks, dominant themes and empirical gaps, providing a clear view of the field’s intellectual foundations. Practical implications Organizations can use these insights to strategically adopt artificial intelligence in ways that enhance environmental performance while mitigating governance and implementation risks. Originality/value This study integrates systematic literature review and bibliometric approaches to synthesize a fragmented literature, distinguishing between positive and critical perspectives on artificial intelligence in sustainability. It advances theoretical debates on artificial intelligence and green innovation and offers practical guidance for managers and policymakers aiming to leverage artificial intelligence for responsible value creation.

title: DEVELOPING BUSINESS CULTURE AMONG UNIVERSITY STUDENTS IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: This article examines the development of business culture among students in the context of the digital economy. It highlights the importance of economic thinking, entrepreneurial skills, digital literacy, and business ethics. The paper also analyzes challenges in higher education and proposes measures to strengthen startup ecosystems and enhance practice-oriented approaches.

title: DETECTION OF EARNINGS MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THROUGH DISCRETIONARY LOAN LOSS PROVISIONS AT RURAL BANKS IN WEST JAVA, CENTRAL JAVA, AND EAST JAVA DURING THE SAK EP TRANSITION PERIOD (2023–2025)
summary: This study examines whether the transition from the rule-based PPAP provisioning regime to the judgment-based CKPN regime under the Indonesian Financial Accounting Standards for Private Entities (SAK EP) is accompanied by a change in the intensity of earnings management through discretionary loan loss provisions (DLLP) in rural banks (Bank Perekonomian Rakyat/BPR). The novelty of the study lies in using 2023–2025 as a transition window that combines the last two years of the PPAP regime and the first year of the CKPN regime in a single sample, allowing the link between the scope of accounting discretion and income smoothing to be observed among small, unlisted banks, a segment rarely examined in the bank earnings management literature. Panel data of 556 conventional BPRs (1,649 bank-year observations) in West Java, Central Java, and East Java are analysed using a two-stage estimation approach. The results show that non-performing loans are an important determinant of loan loss provisions, whereas pre-managed earnings are positively associated with DLLP, consistent with income smoothing. This association is weak under the PPAP regime but becomes markedly stronger in the first year of CKPN adoption, accompanied by a higher share of banks showing strong discretion, mostly in the form of over-provisioning. The findings enrich positive accounting theory by suggesting that the intensity of income smoothing is not constant but is associated with the scope of judgment permitted by accounting standards, and they offer implications for risk-based supervision by OJK and LPS during the early implementation of SAK EP.

title: The role of institutional elements in enterprise innovation resilience: Explainable machine learning evidence from China
summary: Abstract The institutional environment is an important external condition shaping enterprise innovation resilience ( EIR ), particularly enterprises’ capacity to sustain innovation and adapt to external shocks. Yet existing studies have largely focused on single institutional factors or linear average effects, leaving the relative importance, nonlinear patterns, and interactions of multidimensional institutional elements ( IE ) underexplored. Drawing on institutional theory and a sample of Chinese listed agriculture- and forestry-related enterprises, this study combines multiple machine-learning algorithms, including CatBoost, with SHAP to examine how regulative, normative, and cognitive IE predict one-period-ahead enterprise innovation resilience ( EIR t+1 ). The results show that current-period enterprise innovation resilience ( EIR t ) is the strongest predictor of EIR t+1 , indicating pronounced dynamic persistence. Among the three institutional dimensions, environmental governance ( RG ), institutional investor shareholding ( INST ), and innovation culture ( EIC ) are the most important predictive features, while the Cognitive Institutional Index ( CII ) has the highest predictive importance among the three composite institutional indices. IE also exhibit nonlinear, stage-dependent, and cross-dimensional interaction patterns, with substantial heterogeneity across regions, ownership types, enterprise sizes, and agriculture- versus forestry-related enterprises. These findings extend institutional theory to EIR research and highlight the predictive relevance of multidimensional, nonlinear, and context-dependent institutional configurations.

title: All roads lead to Rome: antecedent configurations of green innovation and firm performance from a sustainable business models perspective
summary: Green innovation, pivotal for both business performance and ecological sustainability, remains an enigmatic aspect within sustainable business models (SBMs). Current literature lacks clarity on the SBM configurations that catalyze green innovation and its firm performance implications, necessitating a more profound inquiry. This study presents a dual-study approach with a mixed-methods design to dissect these relationships. Leveraging data from 241 Chinese manufacturers, we first apply Fuzzy Set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fs-QCA) to uncover that no single SBM factor is indispensable for green innovation. Instead, four distinct SBM configurations—Policy Incentive, Policy Coercion, Technology-Driven, and Technology Rent-Seeking—emerge as conducive to green innovation. Further analysis using Propensity Score Matching confirms that these configurations significantly enhance firm performance, indicating diverse effective pathways for green innovation adoption. This research enriches the discourse on green innovation by providing a nuanced configurational perspective, challenging traditional analyses, and expanding theoretical insights in the field.

title: Corporate Governance and Financial Transparency in Indian Companies
summary: Corporate governance and financial transparency determine whether investors, lenders and the public can trust a company with their resources. This project examines how these two concepts have developed and operate in Indian companies, with particular emphasis on listed public companies. The study begins by explaining the concepts and the principal theories, namely agency, stewardship, stakeholder and principal-principal perspectives. It then traces the evolution of Indian governance norms from the voluntary code of the Confederation of Indian Industry and the work of the Birla, Naresh Chandra, Narayana Murthy, Irani and Kotak committees to the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015. The report analyses board structure, independent directors, committees, related party transactions, whistle-blowing, financial reporting under Ind AS, auditor independence and the role of the National Financial Reporting Authority. Five cases, namely Satyam, Tata Sons, IL&FS, the Infosys whistle-blower complaints and Think & Learn, are used to illustrate how failures arise and how regulation has responded. The study concludes that India's legal framework is now broadly comparable to that of leading economies, but that concentrated ownership, doubtful independence of directors, slow enforcement and formalistic compliance continue to limit its effectiveness. It recommends measures to strengthen independent directors, audit quality, enforcement, related party oversight and whistle-blower protection. Keywords: corporate governance, financial transparency, SEBI, Companies Act 2013, independent directors, audit, Ind AS, India.

title: 2026 Credit Union & Fintech AI Search Visibility Study: Measuring Total Brand Omission and Cross-Engine Disagreement Across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Claude
summary: EquiSchema AI LLC conducted a 960-evaluation empirical benchmark study and an 80-prompt cross-engine disagreement analysis across the four leading generative AI search platforms (OpenAI ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Perplexity AI, and Anthropic Claude) to measure how often U.S. Credit Unions and mission-driven Financial Technology firms (Fintechs) are recommended when consumers ask unbranded, high-intent financial questions. While prior industry commentary has focused on AI hallucinations or generic brand-awareness prompts, this study measures Total Brand Omission—defined by EquiSchema AI as the complete exclusion of a qualified financial institution from unbranded, bottom-of-funnel borrower and depositor recommendations, leaving the institution with a 0% probability of consumer consideration. KEY EMPIRICAL FINDINGS (REPORT NO. 2026-02): 1. 96.0% Total Brand Omission (922 Omissions / 960 Evaluations): Across 20 real-world consumer borrowing and deposit queries evaluated across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Claude, the 12 audited national credit unions and ethical fintechs achieved only 4.0% aggregate visibility (38 mentions out of 960 opportunities). Audited Credit Unions suffered a 95.0% Total Brand Omission rate (5.0% visibility), while Ethical Fintechs suffered a 97.1% Total Brand Omission rate (2.9% visibility). 2. 0.0% Foundational Deposit Blackout (Q01–Q03): On the three core consumer deposit queries ($10,000 emergency fund high-yield savings, $500/month savings account, and highest 12-month CD rate for $25,000), all 12 audited Credit Unions and Fintechs recorded 0.0% visibility (0 out of 144 evaluations) across all four AI models. 3. 95.7% Cross-Engine Disagreement: Across 336 total recommendation slots (234 unique query-entity pairs), all four AI models agreed on the same financial institution only 3.8% of the time (4.3% including federal FHA mortgage programs). Over two-thirds (68.4%) of recommended institutions were named by only a single AI engine and completely omitted by the other three. 4. Megabank Collapse (5.4%) & Middleman Capture (17.3%): On specific dollar-tier and credit-score transactional prompts, the "Big 4" U.S. Megabanks captured just 5.4% of total AI recommendation slots combined. Meanwhile, 17.3% of all AI recommendation slots bypassed direct depository lenders entirely in favor of lead-generation middlemen, rate aggregators (such as Bankrate, LendingTree, and Credit Karma), and government program acronyms. 5. Loan-Tier Sensitivity Drift ("Slot Roulette") & Liability Refusals: Holding borrower credit score constant (720 FICO) while shifting auto loan size in $10,000 increments ($60,000 vs. $50,000 vs. $40,000) caused 85.7% of recommended lenders (6 of 7) to rotate or vanish across adjacent dollar brackets. Additionally, on credit-tiered auto loan prompts ($60,000 at 720 score and $45,000 at 650 score), Claude refused to recommend any lender (0 mentions) due to unstructured rate sheets failing confidence guardrails. title: The sustainable competitive advantage in the digital economy: value creation versus value recognition
summary: Purpose This study aims to investigate the competitive advantage in the digital economy, focusing on the Standard & Poor’s (Standard & Poor’s Financial Services (S&P) 500 companies. This study uses two measures, the Economic Value Added (EVA), an indicator of value creation and economic excellence, and Total Shareholder Return (TSR), as an indicator of value recognition and financial excellence, integrating business and investment strategy. Design/methodology/approach Recognizing the limitations of TSR as an indicator of corporate effectiveness in allocating capital, it highlights the importance of EVA as a metric of organizations’ economic potency based on a panel data set of 467 S&P 500-listed financial and non-financial companies for the decade 2013–2023. Findings The results indicate that EVA is a good, yet largely overlooked, measure of competitive advantage and capital allocation, serving as a robust antecedent of Wall Street firms’ value creation versus value recognition. Practical implications The study proposes an applied metric that helps business leaders assess how well listed companies create value by allocating capital across business opportunities, and how well that value is reflected in their market valuation. Originality/value The significance of the EVA is particularly evident when considering the competitive advantage of businesses operating at the core of the emergent digital economy and the integration of business and investment strategies in pursuit of superior market returns.

title: CSR and Shared Value Models for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the Philippines: A Scoping Review
summary: Abstract This scoping review systematically examines how Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Creating Shared Value (CSV) are conceptualized, adapted, and implemented among Philippine micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) between 2016 and 2026. MSMEs, which account for 99.6% of registered businesses and employ two-thirds of the national workforce, remain underrepresented in mainstream sustainability scholarship despite their critical role in inclusive development. Guided by Arksey andO’Malley’s (2005) framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, the review synthesizes 62 sources including peer-reviewed studies, government policies, industry reports, and grey literature. Findings reveal that CSR in MSMEs is largely implicit, rooted in cultural values such as bayanihan and pakikisama, while CSV is emerging as a strategic framework linking social impact with business competitiveness. Documented models cluster into compliance, community-embedded, operational shared value, and supply chain collaborative approaches, each yielding economic, social, and environmental outcomes but constrained by scalability, accessibility, and measurement gaps. Evidence highlights positive impacts on profitability, employee welfare, and resource efficiency, yet remains fragmented, with limited regional diversity, gender perspectives, and longitudinal data. The study concludes by identifying priority research directions and recommending policy incentives, localized frameworks, and culturally grounded tools to strengthen MSME contributions to sustainable and inclusive growth.

title: The FinTech-AI Nexus: A Paradigm Shift in Anti-Money Laundering Surveillance and Enforcement
summary: This study examines how the convergence of FinTech capabilities and AI-driven solutions is reshaping Anti-Money Laundering (AML) surveillance and enforcement. Drawing on the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Institutional Theory (IT), it develops a framework to evaluate the role of technological capabilities and institutional pressures (NP) in strengthening AML outcomes. A theoretical model was constructed, and primary data will be collected from AML professionals, FinTech experts, and compliance officers in the banking and financial services. SmartPLS 4 will be applied to test the hypotheses and validate the conceptual model. The study is expected to demonstrate that FinTech and AI capabilities significantly improve AML surveillance efficiency, which in turn enhances enforcement outcomes. Regulatory support is expected to strengthen the link between surveillance and enforcement, while normative pressures may further drive the adoption of technology. The study contributes to digital financial governance by identifying the key enablers and constraints in technology-driven AML practices. The findings provide actionable insights for regulators, financial institutions, and technology developers, emphasizing that while advanced technologies are crucial, effective regulatory support remains essential for maximizing enforcement success and safeguarding financial integrity in the digital age.
