title: Sustainable Agricultural Finance: A Bibliometric and Systematic Literature Review
summary: Sustainable Agricultural Finance refers to financial mechanisms that support environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive, economically viable, and climate-resilient agricultural development. It encompasses agricultural lending, credit, green finance, value-chain finance, blended finance, digital financial services, insurance, and other financing instruments that facilitate sustainable agricultural production and rural development. The bibliometric dataset assembled for this review is anchored in agricultural lending- and credit-related search terminology (Section 3.1) and therefore most comprehensively captures Sustainable Agricultural Finance research situated at the intersection of credit or lending and sustainability; literature centred on stand-alone agricultural insurance, blended-finance vehicles, or green bonds that does not also use lending- or credit-related terms is less fully represented, a boundary discussed further as a limitation. This study aims to examine the evolution, intellectual structure, thematic development, and future research directions of Sustainable Agricultural Finance through a Bibliometric Systematic Literature Review (BSLR) of 366 Scopus-indexed journal articles published from January 2000 to May 2026. Guided by the PRISMA 2020 framework, it integrates bibliometric analysis using Biblioshiny and VOSviewer with a systematic review. The findings reveal a marked increase in scholarly attention since 2016, with research evolving from conventional agricultural credit and rural finance towards broader themes including sustainability, climate change adaptation, digital finance, green finance, climate-smart agriculture, and sustainable development. The review identifies policy support, digital financial services, value-chain financing, green finance, and social capital as key drivers of Sustainable Agricultural Finance, while highlighting persistent barriers such as information asymmetry, climate risk, inadequate collateral, limited financial literacy, gender disparities, and institutional constraints. Based on these findings, the study proposes a conceptual framework grounded in this credit- and lending-centred evidence base and identifies key research gaps to inform future scholarship, policy formulation, and practice in Sustainable Agricultural Finance.

title: Peran Corporate Governance dalam Meningkatkan Integritas Pelaporan Keuangan: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis atas Dewan Komisaris, Komite Audit, dan Audit Internal
summary: Abstract Objective: This study aims to examine the role of corporate governance in safeguarding financial reporting integrity, with particular emphasis on the board of commissioners, audit committee, and internal audit function. It seeks to identify the governance mechanisms most consistently associated with financial reporting quality and explain the factors underlying variations in empirical findings. Method: This study employs a limited systematic literature review guided by the PRISMA 2020 framework. A total of 39 records were identified through four search queries, of which 13 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the synthesis. The selected studies were analyzed using a narrative-thematic approach to identify recurring patterns, contextual differences, and inconsistencies in the relationships between corporate governance mechanisms and financial reporting integrity. Results: The synthesis reveals three main patterns. First, the audit committee demonstrates the most consistent association with financial reporting quality, particularly through its independence, expertise, size, and meeting frequency. Second, the effectiveness of independent commissioners is contingent on measurement approaches and regulatory contexts. In Indonesian studies, their effect is often statistically insignificant when their proportion merely meets the minimum regulatory threshold. Third, internal audit contributes more effectively to financial reporting oversight when professional competence and independence are present simultaneously, with its effectiveness further strengthened by the involvement of risk oversight committees. Differences in the proxies used to measure financial reporting integrity emerge as a major source of inconsistency across studies. Conclusion/Novelty/Implications: This study proposes a three-layer conceptual framework of financial reporting oversight integrating the board of commissioners, audit committee, and internal audit function. Its contribution lies in explaining how these mechanisms interact and why their effectiveness varies across institutional and measurement contexts. The findings highlight the need to strengthen substantive independence, professional expertise, and coordination among oversight mechanisms rather than relying solely on formal compliance with regulatory requirements. Future research should develop more consistent measures of financial reporting integrity and empirically test the proposed framework across different industries and regulatory settings.

title: The Digital Economy, Globalization and the Development of Trade in Services: Empirical Evidence from a Cross-Country Panel
summary: With rapid digitalization and the expansion of global service trade, whether the digital economy strengthens cross-border service provision has become a central question in international trade. Using a panel of 136 countries over 2012 to 2022, this study constructs a composite Digital Economy Index (DEI) based on four dimensions: digital infrastructure, digital usage and network quality, digital industries and trade, and digital institutions and governance. Employing a two-way fixed effects model with country and year fixed effects and two-way clustered standard errors, we find that digital economy development is associated with a significantly higher share of service trade in GDP. The proposed mechanisms, operating through lower transaction costs, greater service tradability and supply upgrading, and stronger digital governance, are theoretically grounded and find indirect support in the heterogeneity and moderation results. Heterogeneity analysis shows that this association is stronger in countries with more advanced digital foundations, more developed service sectors, and higher government effectiveness. Globalization, measured along economic, social, informational, and financial dimensions, significantly amplifies the relationship, indicating complementarity between digital capability and global connectivity. Across countries, digital development is systematically associated with wider participation in service trade, and the strength of that association is shaped by digital infrastructure, institutional quality, and global integration.

title: Digital Economy and Growth in 58 Economies: The Moderating Role of Financial Development and Human-Capital Investment
summary: The growth payoff of the digital economy may depend on complementary national capacities. This study quantifies the growth effect of deepening the digital economy. It tests how financial development and human-capital investment moderate it in 58 OECD, accession-candidate, key-partner, and EU candidate economies. A composite Digital Economy Index (DEI) aggregates digital-trade participation, infrastructure, and using the Z-score method. The index was computed through 2023, while the estimation covers 2014–2022 owing to the human-capital moderator’s reporting lag. The dependent variable is the natural logarithm of real GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$). Financial development is measured by domestic credit to the private sector (% of GDP) and human-capital investment by government education expenditure (% of GDP). In two-way fixed-effects models, the DEI coefficient is positive but imprecise and is significantly positive at below-average levels of credit and education spending. Within-country digital deepening is robustly positive under country fixed effects. The dividend is smaller where private credit is abundant (“too much finance”). We find no significant interaction with a tertiary-enrolment stock proxy, indicating that moderation operates at the fiscal input margin rather than through the measured skill-stock proxy. The results are robust to instrumentation, aggregation, fixed-effects structure, and sample windows. They are not robust to country-specific linear trends, because these trends absorb most within-country variation in the index during this panel period, rather than necessarily overturning the underlying finding.

title: AI-Driven Technology Decision Intelligence for Human-Centered Digital Transformation
summary: The Technology Decision Intelligence Engine (TDIE): Integrating Outcome Prediction, Readiness and Risk Assessment, Multi-Objective Portfolio Optimization, Explainable AI, and Human-AI Collaborative Decision-Making. Organizations must repeatedly choose among competing technology investments - artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, cloud migration, cybersecurity, data platforms, enterprise system modernization, automation, and workforce training - under binding limits on budget, implementation capacity, skills, time, and risk tolerance. In practice these choices are fragmented across departments, driven by intuition or consultants, and judged by isolated metrics such as return on investment (ROI). This paper proposes the Technology Decision Intelligence Engine (TDIE), an AI-driven decision-support framework that treats technology selection as a constrained portfolio problem rather than a ranking problem. TDIE integrates ten components in a closed loop: an organizational data layer that combines structured data with document understanding; organizational diagnosis of maturity, gaps, and readiness; technology opportunity detection; machine-learning prediction of cost, benefit, adoption probability, and ROI; multi-dimensional readiness and risk assessment; multi-objective portfolio optimization that returns a Pareto set instead of a single score; explainable AI using feature attribution and counterfactuals; structured human-AI collaboration in which managers can accept, modify, or reject recommendations with reasons recorded; and a feedback loop that compares predicted with realized outcomes. The paper specifies a rigorous mathematical formulation, a hybrid AI architecture in which large language models are restricted to extraction and managerial explanation, a defensible dataset strategy that labels synthetic data as synthetic, ten falsifiable experiments, strong baselines including AHP, TOPSIS, and ROI-only ranking, and a full evaluation, ablation, and robustness protocol. Empirical validation is specified as a complete, falsifiable evaluation protocol, so that the framework can be implemented and tested exactly as described.

title: Financial inclusion through FinTech: A bibliometric and systematic review of the intellectual structure and future research agenda
summary: Promoting inclusive economic development and reducing financial exclusion are now strategic objectives for governments, regulators and development agencies. Financial technology (FinTech), including mobile banking, digital payments, peer to peer lending, blockchain and artificial intelligence, has changed how financial services reach underserved groups, especially in emerging economies. This study combines bibliometric analysis with a systematic literature review to map the intellectual structure and recent trends of research on FinTech enabled financial inclusion. The bibliometric analysis covers 219 Scopus records published between 2016 and May 2026, from 122 sources and 661 authors. Publication trends, productive sources and authors, country collaboration, keyword co-occurrence, thematic maps and conceptual structures were analysed with Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer. Following PRISMA 2020, 55 studies were selected for thematic synthesis. The dataset shows rapid growth, with an annual growth rate of 30.66 percent, an average of 28.91 citations per document and 39.27 percent international co authorship. The synthesis identifies six research streams: FinTech adoption and financial inclusion; financial literacy and digital inclusion; MSME development and entrepreneurship; women’s empowerment, trust and digital inclusion; sustainability and inclusive development; and AI and blockchain based financial ecosystems. The literature generally links FinTech with better access to and use of financial services, but the benefits depend on literacy, trust, infrastructure and regulation. The study proposes an integrated conceptual framework and a research agenda covering longitudinal evidence, digitally excluded populations, sustainability outcomes and responsible use of AI and blockchain. The findings guide researchers, policymakers, regulators and FinTech practitioners.

title: The Role of Digital Government Development and Fintech in Enhancing Urban Economic Resilience
summary: This study asks whether digital government strengthens urban economic resilience and whether fintech amplifies this effect. Using balanced panel data for 295 Chinese prefecture-level and above cities from 2018–2023, we estimate two-way fixed-effects models. Digital government is positively associated with urban economic resilience, and the relationship remains stable across reported robustness checks. Channel tests show positive associations with financial activity and government intervention, while fintech significantly strengthens the digital government–resilience relationship. Effects are more pronounced in eastern and highly open cities. The findings identify digital governance and fintech as complementary capabilities for resilient urban development.

title: Green finance policy and environmental decoupling: evidence from China
summary: As a policy instrument designed to promote coordinated economic growth and environmental protection in China, the Green Finance Reform and Innovation Pilot Zones (GFP) may play an important role in fostering environmental decoupling, yet their effectiveness remains unclear. This article provides new evidence on the effectiveness of China’s green finance policy by examining its effects on carbon decoupling and haze decoupling. Using balanced panel data of Chinese cities from 2012 to 2021, we employ a difference-in-differences (DID) model and find that GFP promotes carbon decoupling but has no significant effect on haze decoupling. Mechanism analysis reveals that green innovation, green bond development, and environmental regulation are important channels through which GFP promotes carbon decoupling. Further analyses show that the carbon decoupling effect is more pronounced in regions with higher levels of financial technology (Fintech) development and greater public environmental concern. Moreover, GFP also generates special spatial spillover effects, promoting carbon decoupling in neighbouring areas. These findings have important policy implications for enhancing the environmental effectiveness of China’s green finance policy.

title: Exploring High School Students’ Individual Political Culture in the Context of Digital Transformation
summary: Political culture plays an important role in students’ socialization and preparation for civic life. In the context of digital transformation, adolescents increasingly encounter political information through online platforms, which creates new opportunities for civic learning but also raises concerns about fragmented understanding and uncritical information consumption. This study examines high school students’ individual political culture by exploring their understanding of political culture, the rule of law and civil society, their sources of political information they report and their perceptions of the influence of these sources, and their views on the importance of civic and political participation in society. A qualitative content analysis was conducted between September and December 2025 with 960 high school students from five cities in Kazakhstan. Data were collected through four open-ended questionnaire questions and analysed using inductive qualitative content analysis, followed by descriptive frequency analysis of semantic units, codes, and categories. The findings indicate that students predominantly conceptualised political culture in cognitive-evaluative and attitudinal terms, while their understanding of the rule of law and civil society was mainly expressed through legal foundations and norms. Digital and online media were the most frequently reported sources of political information, while family, traditional media, and educational resources were mentioned less frequently. Students generally recognised the importance of civic participation, particularly for democratic development, social integration, and influence on public decision-making. The findings highlight the need to strengthen media literacy, critical evaluation of political information, and practice-oriented civic education within digitally transformed educational environments. title: Beyond Compliance: ESG-Driven Workplace Transformation, Green HRM, and Employee Wellness as Pathways to Sustainable Public Sector Success
summary: Growing calls for the implementation of ESG principles within the core operations of the public sector indicate the necessity to go beyond the superficiality of formal compliance and make ESG an integral component of the organization’s transformation. The purpose of this conceptual paper is to analyze the complex connection between ESG-induced changes in the workplace, Green Human Resource Management (Green HRM), and employees’ well-being suggesting that the combination of those three factors is essential for sustainable performance of organizations. Using Ability-Motivation-Opportunity (AMO) framework and Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory, we hypothesize that Green HRM practices play the key mediating role between organizational ESG strategy and individual well-being, leading to improved environmental and social performance. We will conduct an integrative literature review along with the analysis of illustrative examples from UK’s National Health Service and the City of Vancouver, showing the two-sided nature of green work transformation which can be perceived either as a job resource or a job demand. This paper disputes the common assumption that the interests of environmental programs and employee welfare are conflicting in nature, as opposed to being complementary through participatory design, green transformational leadership, and holistic governance orientation. Our paper presents practical suggestions for public sector leaders to collaboratively create a workplace environment that sustains both the Earth and its people, and also presents a crucial research agenda to test these dynamics within a sector known for bureaucratic inefficiency.

title: Accounting research in Nazi Germany: Analysis of German academic business journals from 1929 to 1945
summary: This study investigates accounting research during the Nazi era by analysing articles published in three major German academic business journals of that time. We identify 1013 accounting articles from 1929 to 1945 and contextualise the research using a sociology of science perspective. Our findings reveal that after the Nazi seizure of power in 1933, accounting research retained its application-oriented focus but increasingly aligned with ideological views, including topics reflecting anti-liberal Nazi doctrines such as price regulation and changes in accounting education and corporate governance. Scientific norms and values were restricted in many ways, and accounting research had to subordinate itself to the regime. Already existing ethical-normative research approaches gained importance. While most authors used a more factual, technocratic language, others demonstrated closer alignment with Nazi rhetoric. Instances of author discrimination were identified, but explicit reproaches remained rare.

title: Interest rate liberalization and bank resource allocation efficiency: evidence from China
summary: The market-oriented reform of interest rates is one of the most significant transformations in China’s financial system. Its impact on banks’ resource allocation efficiency at the micro level warrants close examination. Based on an unbalanced panel dataset of 314 Chinese commercial banks from 2007 to 2022, this paper empirically investigates the effect of interest rate liberalization on the efficiency of resource allocation in commercial banks, as well as the heterogeneity of this effect. The findings are as follows: First, the relationship between interest rate liberalization and bank resource allocation efficiency exhibits a pronounced U-shaped pattern, with two critical threshold values. When the interest rate liberalization index is below 0.460, marketization suppresses bank resource allocation efficiency. When the index lies between 0.460 and 0.501, the negative impact intensifies. However, once the index exceeds the critical threshold of 0.501, interest rate liberalization begins to significantly enhance efficiency. This dynamic evolution confirms the pattern of “reform pain followed by institutional dividend”. Second, the heterogeneity analysis reveals several important insights. Banks with high levels of innovation experience short-term pressure but exhibit 69.2% greater long-term elasticity in efficiency recovery compared to their low-innovation counterparts, underscoring the strategic value of financial innovation during the deepening phase of interest rate liberalization. In regions with higher degrees of marketization, efficiency improves 54.7% faster due to institutional advantages, providing empirical evidence for the “institutional environment as a reform accelerator” hypothesis. More importantly, banks in regions with higher levels of green finance improve their efficiency at a rate 2.1 times faster than those in regions with lower green finance development. This indicates that interest rate liberalization not only serves as a tool for enhancing bank resource allocation efficiency, but also provides a vital institutional foundation for channeling financial resources toward key areas of sustainable development.

title: Integrating Digital Transformation into Strategic Management: Pathways for Cooperative Growth in Region IV-A
summary: This study examined the strategic management practices of primary cooperatives in Region IV-A CALABARZON, emphasizing their adaptation to digital transformation and the potential integration of digital technologies into cooperative operations. Specifically, it assessed internal strategic processes, external environmental influences, digital readiness, and the acceptability of a proposed user-friendly digital platform. Employing a mixed-methods research design, quantitative data were collected from 339 cooperative members and 31 management personnel across Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal, and Quezon, supplemented by structured interviews with selected cooperative leaders. Data were analyzed using frequency, weighted mean, analysis of variance (ANOVA), and Pearson correlation. Findings revealed that most cooperatives had operated for over ten years, demonstrating steady capital growth, substantial membership, and strong capabilities in goal setting and governance. However, limitations emerged in strategy implementation and digital technology adoption. Technological advancements and regulatory changes significantly influenced strategic decision-making, while cooperative operational longevity was associated with selected strategic management practices. The proposed digital platform received favorable evaluations regarding usability, satisfaction, and perceived usefulness. Nevertheless, limited internet connectivity, financial constraints, inadequate digital literacy, cybersecurity concerns, and organizational resistance remained significant barriers. Despite these challenges, digital transformation presented opportunities to improve operational efficiency, service delivery, and digital payment integration. The study concluded that cooperatives in CALABARZON remain in the early stages of digital transformation. Consequently, sustained digital capacity-building, stakeholder training, supportive regulatory policies, and customized technological solutions are recommended to strengthen cooperative sustainability, organizational responsiveness, strategic management effectiveness, and long-term competitiveness in an increasingly digital business environment.

title: The Evolution of Corporate Governance: A Comparative Study of the Cadbury Committee Report (1992), Sarbanes-Oxley Act (2002), and the Indian Corporate Governance Framework
summary: Corporate governance has emerged as a critical mechanism for ensuring accountability, transparency, and sustainable value creation in modern corporations, particularly in the wake of high-profile corporate failures that exposed weaknesses in board oversight, financial reporting, and internal controls. This study undertakes a comparative analysis of three landmark frameworks: the Cadbury Report (1992) of the United Kingdom, the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (2002) of the United States, and the contemporary Indian corporate governance regime anchored in the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI regulations. The purpose is to examine the evolution of core governance principles, especially board independence, the role and composition of audit committees, and mechanisms of corporate accountability, across different institutional and regulatory contexts. Major findings indicate that while the Cadbury Report laid foundational voluntary principles centred on board structure and financial integrity, Sarbanes-Oxley introduced rigorous, mandatory internal-control and certification requirements, and the Indian framework has synthesised both approaches into a hybrid model that balances statutory mandates with market-oriented disclosure norms. The study concludes that corporate governance has evolved from principle-based, comply-or-explain systems toward more prescriptive, enforcement-oriented regimes, yet retains a common emphasis on independent oversight and accountability as universal safeguards against managerial opportunism.

title: Twin transformation – an empirical analysis of the interplay between sustainability and digital transformation in German legacy media companies
summary: Sustainability and digitalisation are two transformations reshaping the economy, ecology, politics, and society. Their synergy, known as twin transformation, is becoming increasingly important for decision-makers and academia. This study examines twin transformation in large German legacy media companies through document analysis and qualitative expert interviews. Media companies are of particular interest due to their dual role as both sustainable actors and influential communicators, influencing public perception while navigating complex digital shifts. The results indicate that sustainability and digital transformation are predominantly approached separately in German legacy media, with only a few projects embodying the twin transformation approach. Structural decentralisation, regulatory gaps, and fragmented IT systems present major challenges to implementation. Nevertheless, the interviewees regard twin transformation as a valuable, though organisationally demanding, approach to business development.

title: Manufacturing as a Service: A Survey on Enabling Flexible, Sustainable, and Intelligent Production Through Digital Transformation
summary: Manufacturing as a Service (MaaS) has emerged as a transformative paradigm at the intersection of Industry 4.0 and servitization, enabling flexible, sustainable, and intelligent production through on-demand provisioning of manufacturing resources. By leveraging cyber–physical systems, the Industrial Internet of Things, cloud/edge computing, artificial intelligence, digital twins, and data spaces, MaaS platforms decouple production capacity from asset ownership and orchestrate distributed manufacturing ecosystems in a service-oriented manner. This survey provides a structured, expert-driven review of the MaaS landscape, covering its conceptual foundations, stakeholder ecosystem, and introducing a reference architecture structured around data management, modeling, and decision-making suites. We analyze enabling technologies such as data spaces, asset administration shell, knowledge graphs, intent-based servitization, AI-driven prediction, and formal modeling approaches including linear, discrete-event, and hybrid systems. Furthermore, we examine optimization, planning and scheduling, digital twins, cloud manufacturing orchestration, and Zero-X evaluation frameworks targeting zero defects, zero downtime, zero waste, and zero emissions. Finally, we identify key open challenges related to scalability, interoperability, trust, data sovereignty, small–medium enterprise adoption, and circularity, outlining future research directions toward robust and trustworthy MaaS ecosystems.

title: ESG in Financial Markets and Corporate Practice: Teaching Why Acting Together Is Hard with Three Games on Enforcement, Verification, and Common Knowledge
summary: Corporate ESG commitments and claims can fail for the same reasons as collective action initiatives for sustainability, yet classroom games usually teach only one of them, the free-rider problem. This paper argues that collective action fails for three distinct reasons and proposes a short game for each. A cheating game, a public goods game played without and then with monitoring, teaches the enforcement gap: contributing is efficient but not individually rational unless non-contribution is detected and sanctioned. A bluffing game, in which firms claim to be green, teaches the verification gap: when claims are free, the word “green” earns no premium until verification makes false claims costly. A hats puzzle followed by a stag hunt teaches the common knowledge gap: conditional cooperation requires that everyone knows that everyone knows, so compliance must be visible. Each game is mapped to the institution that closes its gap, and each gap has a counterpart in corporate practice and financial markets, from net-zero pledges without penalties and unverified ESG disclosures to ESG ratings that coordinate investors’ beliefs. The paper provides payoff tables, equilibrium predictions, debriefing questions, and a teaching note for a 90 min session. The proposal has not yet been evaluated in a classroom.

title: Digital Transformation of Labor Welfare and Social Security Policies in India: An Analysis of Social Security Cards
summary: India’s labour market includes a large population of workers in informal, temporary, migrant, construction, self-employed, gig and platform occupations. For these workers, access to welfare programmes has historically been affected by fragmented records, mobility, lack of awareness and complex administrative procedures. Digital transformation is changing this delivery environment by creating interoperable databases, digital identities, online registration, electronic authentication and integrated service platforms. This paper analyses the role of social security cards and digital worker identification, with particular focus on the e-Shram portal. The study uses a descriptive and analytical review of government documents and international literature. e-Shram creates a National Database of Unorganised Workers and provides a digital identity through which workers can be connected with welfare and social-security schemes. The paper argues that digital identification can improve portability, targeting, record management and awareness, but registration alone does not guarantee effective coverage. Digital exclusion, data privacy, cyber security, language barriers, inaccurate records and limited digital literacy remain important challenges. The paper recommends assisted digital access, regular data updating, strong privacy safeguards, multilingual services, interoperability and outcome-based monitoring. Digital systems should therefore complement, rather than replace, accessible physical institutions and worker-centred welfare administration.

title: An approach to assessing the risks of restaurant businesses based on a scientific and methodological framework in the context of the industry’s digital transformation
summary: The article substantiates the need for a special approach to risk assessment in the restaurant business in the context of the digital transformation of the industry. A study of current digitalization trends in public catering has made it possible to identify new categories of risks caused by the introduction of digital technologies: technological, operational, regulatory, and reputational. The author presents an original methodology that combines traditional risk management with industry-specific features and digital factors. The methodological framework relies on multi-factor analysis, a risk matrix, and scenario modeling. The proposed risk assessment matrix can be practically applied by restaurant enterprises in building risk management systems.

title: CORPORATE CULTURE AND EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT IN IN THE CONTEXT OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION: EVIDENCE FROM COAL MINING ENTERPRISES IN VIETNAM
summary: In the context of digital transformation, employee engagement has become a crucial factor for workforce stability, operational efficiency, and sustainable development, particularly in high-risk industries such as coal mining. This study examines the effect of corporate culture on employee engagement in coal mining enterprises in Vietnam and investigates the moderating role of digital transformation readiness. Data were collected through direct surveys of 356 employees and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The results indicate that corporate culture has a positive and statistically significant effect on employee engagement. Digital transformation readiness positively moderates this relationship, suggesting that the effect of corporate culture on employee engagement becomes stronger when enterprises demonstrate higher readiness for digital transformation. The model explains 66.7% of the variance in employee engagement. The findings contribute empirical evidence from a traditional high-risk industry undergoing digital transformation and provide managerial implications for strengthening employee engagement through cultural development and digital readiness.

title: Barriers, Risks, and Critical Success Factors of Digital Transformation Initiatives on Organisational Performance in the Nigerian Banking Industry
summary: This study examines the barriers, risks, and critical success factors (CSFs) of digital transformation (DT) initiatives and their relationship with organisational performance across Nigerian deposit money banks (DMBs). The investigation adopts a dual-strand methodology combining an integrative systematic review, reported in strict alignment with the PRISMA 2020 framework, with descriptive financial analyses of seven listed commercial banks over the 2019–2024 financial quinquennium, complemented by aggregate clearing and settlement metrics from the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS). Systematic literature searches across public repositories and citation reference tracking yielded 35 records, of which 16 met the defined eligibility criteria and were synthesised. Cybersecurity was identified as the predominant operational and strategic risk (4 of 16 studies; 25.0%), whilst robust cybersecurity frameworks and modernised technology/digital infrastructure constituted the most prominent CSFs (4 of 16 studies each; 25.0%). Human and cultural barriers represented the most frequently identified impediment (3 of 16 studies; 18.8%), followed closely by infrastructural and technological constraints (2 of 16 studies; 12.5%). Among the six empirical studies examining financial outcomes, two established positive and statistically significant associations with return on assets (ROA), one documented mixed outcomes varying by payment channel, one observed an insignificant effect, and two did not report confirmed directional estimates. Across five banks with continuous longitudinal disclosures, mean ROA rose from 2.48% in 2019 to 3.48% in 2024. However, because this interval was marked by acute macroeconomic shocks, including substantial naira devaluations, elevated inflation, and foreign exchange (FX) revaluation gains, this profitability growth cannot be causally attributed to digital transformation on available evidence. The study recommends that the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) institute a regulatory sandbox conditioned upon stringent cybersecurity prerequisites, issue cyber-resilience benchmarks, and mandate disaggregated reporting of foreign exchange revaluation gains versus core operational earnings.

title: Organizational and managerial support for the development of the innovation and investment potential of food industry enterprises in the context of digital transformation
summary: The article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations for establishing the organizational and managerial framework needed to develop enterprises’ innovation and investment potential in the context of digital transformation. The study substantiates the need for a comprehensive approach to managing innovation and investment potential – one that aligns resource capabilities, organizational mechanisms, managerial competencies, and digital tools. The study synthesizes scientific approaches to defining the essence of innovation and investment potential and clarifies the organizational and managerial support for them. The system comprises six interconnected components: strategic-managerial, organizational-structural, human resource/competency-based, information-digital, investment-coordination, and control-adaptation. The functional purpose of each component is defined, and the necessity for their coordinated interaction is established to ensure the strategic orientation of innovation and investment processes. Factors influencing the differentiation of organizational and managerial support are systematized into three groups: industry-technological, intra-organizational, and external environmental. An organizational and managerial framework for developing the innovation and investment potential of enterprises – specifically tailored for the food industry – is formulated, illustrating the interrelationships among the identified factors, system components, and managerial tools. The proposed approach creates the prerequisites for adapting management mechanisms to enterprises’ technological specifics, resource capabilities, and operational risks, thereby improving performance in innovation and investment activities, technological modernization, the digitalization of business processes, and the development of sustainable competitive advantages. title: Beyond AI Adoption: A Human-Centred Decision Intelligence Framework for Sustainable Digital Transformation of French SMEs
summary: An AI-Driven Strategic Technology Management Approach for Improving Investment Decisions, Productivity, Cyber Resilience and Business Competitiveness. Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are under simultaneous pressure to adopt artificial intelligence (AI), to protect themselves against rising cyber risk, and to reduce the cost and environmental footprint of their operations. Yet the decisions that govern these investments are still commonly made with vendor claims, intuition and spreadsheets, because the analytical machinery of large corporations is neither affordable nor usable at SME scale. This paper argues that the binding problem is not AI adoption but AI investment decision quality, and it proposes a remedy: a human-centred decision intelligence framework, TDIE-SME, that extends the Technology Decision Intelligence Engine (TDIE) to the specific conditions of French SMEs. The framework assesses any candidate technology across five dimensions - AI investment intelligence, SME digital transformation, cyber and technology risk intelligence, human-AI management, and sustainable technology strategy - and integrates multi-criteria decision analysis, predictive analytics and explainable AI behind a human-in-the-loop review gate. For each candidate technology it produces a five-part decision: whether to adopt, defer or reject; the expected financial return; the financial, operational and cyber risk profile; the readiness of people and organisation; and the expected effect on sustainability and competitiveness. The paper specifies the framework's architecture, indicators and decision pipeline, illustrates its use on a clearly hypothetical scenario, and sets out a six-stage research programme - including a minimum viable prototype of a decision intelligence dashboard, presently under development - through which the framework is to be empirically evaluated. No empirical results are claimed at this stage; the contribution is the framework, its decision logic, and a falsifiable evaluation design.

title: Beyond the basics: how digital transformation, orientation and competence fuel SME performance through resilience in the manufacturing sector
summary: Purpose In emerging economies such as Pakistan, SMEs have a high failure rate, underscoring the need to understand what drives SME performance. This paper fills a knowledge gap by considering the impact of digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and entrepreneurial resilience on SMEs' performance. Entrepreneurial resilience serves as a mediator between digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and SME performance. Finally, environmental dynamism (ED) is used as a moderator between entrepreneurial resilience and SMEs' performance. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 453 managers of manufacturing SMEs in Punjab, Pakistan. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling is used for hypothesis testing. Findings Digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation and entrepreneurial competencies have a significant and positive influence on entrepreneurial resilience and SME performance. Entrepreneurial resilience significantly enhances SMEs' performance. Additionally, entrepreneurial resilience significantly mediates the relationships among digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competencies and SME performance. Finally, ED significantly moderates the relationship between entrepreneurial resilience and SMEs' performance. Practical implications SME managers should prioritize digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, competence, resilience and ED to measure SMEs' performance. Policymakers can support these efforts by developing adaptive frameworks that enable SMEs to remain competitive in dynamic environments. Originality/value This is initial research that integrates digital transformation, entrepreneurial orientation, entrepreneurial competence, entrepreneurial resilience and ED to examine SME performance within the resource orchestration theory (ROT).

title: Trade Tariffs and Corporate Greenwashing: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Firms
summary: Using data on Chinese A-share firms from 2009 to 2023, we examine how import tariff exposure is related to corporate greenwashing. We combine tariff and customs data with annual reports and environmental penalty records. Greenwashing is measured by the gap between environmental disclosure and penalties relative to peers. Random-effects logit estimates show that lower tariff exposure is associated with a higher likelihood of this gap. This relationship varies with media attention, managerial incentives, and fund occupation. The findings do not prove that firms intend to mislead or that tariffs improve the environment.

title: Lost in translation: financial barriers to new technologies
summary: Advanced economies are reshaped by transitions from old to new technological paradigms. These transitions rely on complementary innovations that spread new technologies across industries. What happens when a financial crisis disrupts investment in these innovations? Using a Schumpeterian endogenous growth model with financial frictions, we show that investment in new technologies is more sensitive to tighter financial conditions than investment in mature technologies. The key mechanism is path dependence: firms build expertise in the technologies they previously developed, leading young firms to self-select into emerging technologies. As young firms are more financially constrained, shocks to financing disproportionately depress innovation in new technologies. We validate this mechanism using causal evidence on green patenting by German firms around the Global Financial Crisis. The aggregate fraction of patenting in carbon reducing technologies stagnated after the crisis. Quantifying our model using the causal estimates from the micro data implies that the slowdown of the sorting of young firms into new technologies accounts for about a fifth of the macro trends in such green innovation.

title: How does Artificial Intelligence Impact Social Commerce in the Era of Digital Transformation? A Systematic Review and Research Agenda for a Sustainable Future
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to transform social commerce (S-commerce), changing how businesses interact with customers, personalising customer experiences, and optimising their operations. This study identifies recent AI developments and their impact on S-commerce through a systematic literature review, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 as a guideline. In the review, 51 articles are extracted from the Web of Science database and used for thematic analysis, revealing that AI developments, combined with machine learning and natural language processing capabilities, have refined personalisation in S-commerce. At the same time, although digital assistants powered by AI are helping consumers make decisions, important ethical and privacy-related issues have arisen. Ultimately, the success of AI integration into S-commerce platforms depends on consumer engagement and satisfaction. Based on the review, the study presents a conceptual model that synthesises five themes capturing AI’s role in S-commerce: personalisation, consumer engagement, recommendation systems, ethical and privacy considerations, and contributions to sustainable S-commerce. Potential gaps in the literature provide the basis for a structured future research agenda on AI-enabled social commerce.

title: Advancing sustainable financing through pandemic bond: a Bayesian model averaging approach to liquidity premia
summary: Abstract Pandemic bonds, as a subtype of catastrophe (CAT) bonds, are designed to transfer public health risks to capital markets, yet they face substantial liquidity risk due to their nascent market structure and limited risk design. Using a relatively small sample from 2020 to 2024, we apply Bayesian model averaging (BMA) and interpretable machine learning (IML) to examine the associations of macroeconomic and bond-specific characteristics with liquidity premia across market phases. We find that the average liquidity premium of natural catastrophe bonds (1364 bps) is substantially higher than that of pandemic bonds (452 bps), potentially reflecting differences in bond characteristics and contractual structures. The estimates suggest that higher ESG scores and higher disclosed health scores are associated with lower estimated pandemic-bond premia, with health-score categories receiving slightly greater posterior inclusion support than ESG in the joint specification. Pandemic bond premia are higher during hard market phases, while several predictors receive greater posterior inclusion support during soft markets. Overall, the results suggest that incorporating a health-specific index, alongside insights from traditional CAT and green bond design, could enhance the resilience of pandemic bonds and strengthen their role in sustainable development.

title: From Global Emergence to Local Anchorage: Evolution of the CSR Concept, Morocco's Commitment and Integration into the Educational System
summary: Since the 20th century, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has been widely explored by researchers and practitioners across different contexts. Over time, the concept has evolved into a complex and multidimensional framework, characterized by diverse interpretations and the absence of a unified theoretical consensus. While industrialized countries began to engage with CSR as early as the 1950s, Morocco’s commitment to sustainability emerged later. However, recent years have been marked by increasing awareness and growing momentum, reflected in the introduction of CSR labels, charters, and responsible practices within companies and institutions.CSR has become a central topic at academic, economic, and social levels. This article reviews the evolution of CSR and examines Morocco's efforts to integrate sustainability into its national policies and strategies. It also examines the extent to which sustainability is incorporated into the Moroccan education system.. By exploring the link between CSR, public policy, and education through this lens, this study provides insights into how Morocco is working to build a sustainable culture of responsibility at the national level, and identifies the institutional conditions under which such efforts are more or less likely to translate into practice. title: False Green, True Damage: The Erosion of Supplier Sustainability Through Greenwashing Spillovers in Supply Chains
summary: ABSTRACT Using matched supplier–client data of Chinese A‐share listed companies (2009–2024), we examine how client greenwashing affects suppliers' green total factor productivity (GTFP). We find that client greenwashing significantly suppresses suppliers' GTFP, indicating that downstream firms' selective environmental communication can translate into real efficiency losses in upstream green production. This effect mainly operates through a weakened information environment and reduced supplier green efforts. Further analyses show that the effect is stronger when dependence asymmetry is more pronounced or more difficult to mitigate, namely when clients have greater market influence, when client information transparency is lower, or when suppliers have a lower degree of digital transformation. Our findings reveal that selective environmental communication generates spillover effects beyond disclosing firms, adversely impacting suppliers' green development.

title: Financial Technology and Financial Inclusion: Evidence from East African Community Member Countries
summary: This study examines the effect of financial technology on financial inclusion in the eight East African Community member countries over 2014–2023, using a balanced panel of 80 country-year observations. Fintech is measured by penetration rate, usage rate and transaction intensity (mobile-money transactions per adult), with GDP per capita, inflation, financial literacy and bank-branch density as controls. Panel unit root and Kao cointegration tests are reported, and random-effects and fixed-effects estimators are compared with the Hausman test (χ²(5) = 4.79, p = 0.441), with two-way fixed effects, first differences and correlated random effects as robustness checks. Penetration rate (β = 4.965, p = 0.002) and transaction intensity (β = 4.552, p = 0.001) have positive significant effects that survive the controls and fixed effects, whereas usage rate has no significant independent effect; GDP per capita is the strongest control. Fintech advances inclusion through breadth of access and economically meaningful transaction use rather than frequency of use: repeated low-value transfers do not connect users to formal savings, credit or insurance. Because the effects reflect long-run co-movement rather than year-to-year changes, they are interpreted as long-run associations. Policy should prioritise affordable access, interoperable payments and bank–fintech partnerships that convert activity into formal participation. JEL classification numbers: G21, G23, O16, O33, O55. title: OWNERSHIP STRUCTURE AND EARNINGS MANAGEMENT PRACTICES OF LISTED CONSUMER GOODS FIRMS IN NIGERIA
summary: This research investigated the influence of ownership structure on earnings management within publicly traded consumer goods companies in Nigeria. The study specifically examined the impact of director ownership, institutional ownership, and block ownership on earnings management. The research utilised an ex-post facto design and leveraged panel data from the annual reports of 16 selected enterprises out of a total of 21 consumer goods firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX) for the period 2015– 2024. Earnings management was assessed by discretionary accruals derived from the Modified Jones Model (1995). Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, diagnostic assessments, and panel regression methodologies were utilised for data analysis. The results indicated that director ownership exerts a negative and significant influence on earnings management, suggesting that heightened director shareholding limits earnings manipulation. Institutional ownership exhibited a positive yet negligible impact on earnings management, indicating that institutional investors do not substantially affect earnings management methods inside the tested firms. Moreover, block ownership demonstrated a positive and significant influence on earnings management, suggesting that ownership concentration may promote earnings manipulation. The research determines that ownership structure markedly affects profits management techniques within publicly traded consumer goods companies in Nigeria. The study advocates for companies to promote appropriate levels of director ownership to align the interests of management and shareholders, while regulatory bodies should intensify oversight of firms with concentrated ownership structures to safeguard minority shareholders and improve the quality of financial reporting. Keywords: Ownership structure, director ownership, institutional ownership, block ownership, earnings management, consumer goods firms, Nigeria.

title: Role of Corporate Governance in Business Success
summary: Corporate governance has emerged as an essential component of modern business management and sustainable corporate development. It provides a framework through which companies are directed, controlled and held accountable to shareholders and other stakeholders. Effective corporate governance promotes transparency, accountability, ethical decision-making, responsible management and protection of stakeholder interests. In India, the legal framework governing corporate governance has developed significantly through the Companies Act, 2013, the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. These legal mechanisms seek to strengthen the functioning of boards, independent directors, audit committees, disclosure systems and shareholder protection. This paper examines the relationship between corporate governance and business success from a legal and analytical perspective. It argues that corporate governance should not be regarded merely as a compliance requirement but as a strategic mechanism capable of improving investor confidence, reducing corporate risks, preventing fraud, enhancing reputation and promoting long-term business sustainability. The paper further analyses major corporate failures in India to demonstrate the consequences of weak governance and examines the role of transparency, independent oversight and accountability in creating sustainable enterprises. It concludes that effective corporate governance creates value not only for shareholders but also for employees, creditors, consumers and society.

title: System Models and Strategies for Managing Investment and Innovation Development in the Context of Decentralisation Reform
summary: Purpose: The purpose of the study is to investigate the relationships between the level of decentralisation, corporate governance mechanisms and investment activity in the public sector of Ukraine. Design/Methodology/Approach: The methodological basis is system-structural, comparative, and content analyses of secondary data, which provided a comprehensive study of corporate governance in the context of decentralisation. The purposive sample includes 39 scientific publications and analytical reports (2011–2025) and statistical data from international organisations (OECD, World Bank, European Commission) for 2020–2024. Research Limitation: The findings indicate a need for further research that considers regional differences and the long-term effects of decentralisation reforms. Findings: The effectiveness of corporate practices depends directly on the level of institutional autonomy, digital maturity, and partnerships between public and private actors. The proposed analytical model formalised direct and indirect connections between decentralisation, corporate mechanisms and investment activity. Fiscal autonomy and polycentric management create conditions for expanding community investment opportunities, but uneven resource bases and insufficient human resources limit their effectiveness. Practical Implication: The proposed model can support strategic planning, increase transparency in management decisions, and strengthen corporate responsibility in the public sector. Social Implication: The results contribute to sustainable regional development by supporting more effective public governance under decentralisation. Originality/Value: Unlike studies that examine these variables separately, the model shows direct and indirect links between the level of decentralisation and investment activity through corporate governance mechanisms, moderated by political stability, the rule of law and European integration, for Ukraine under martial law.

title: Does Corporate Accountability Towards Biodiversity Loss and Species Extinction Protection Account for Audit Efforts: New Insights from External Auditing
summary: This study investigates whether and how corporate biodiversity disclosure affects external audit efforts. Using a deep‐learning‐expanded text analysis of corporate social responsibility reports for heavily polluting Chinese companies from 2009 to 2021, this paper examines the relation between biodiversity disclosure and audit efforts. The empirical evidence reveals that firms with more extensive biodiversity disclosure exhibit significantly greater external audit efforts. The results remain robust to a series of endogeneity checks, including two‐stage least squares estimation and a combined propensity score matching and difference‐in‐differences analysis. Further analyses show that this positive relation is more pronounced for non‐state‐owned enterprises and firms located in eastern China. Mechanism tests reveal that biodiversity disclosure by heavy polluters triggers a ‘horn effect’, which elevates auditors' perceptions of composite audit risk, thereby driving greater audit effort. Interestingly, while biodiversity disclosures increase audit duration, they do not translate into higher audit fees. Collectively, the findings demonstrate that corporate biodiversity accountability increases audit risk and effort, highlighting the economic consequences of sustainability reporting within the auditing context.

title: Qualité de l'audit légal et régulation du comportement des acteurs de la commande publique : le cas de GECAMINES SA (République Démocratique du Congo)
summary: Résumé Cet article examine dans quelle mesure l’audit légal permet de mettre en évidence le non-respect des procédures de passation des marchés publics et de réguler le comportement des acteurs qui y prennent part, dans une entreprise publique de l’espace OHADA. Il mobilise la définition de la qualité de l’audit de De Angelo (1981), la théorie de l’agence et les travaux sur la gouvernance pour formuler deux hypothèses : la qualité de l’audit, appréciée par la détection et la révélation des anomalies, met en évidence le non-respect des procédures (H1) ; les recommandations du commissaire aux comptes et leur suivi régulent le comportement des acteurs (H2). La démarche est une étude de cas unique, GECAMINES SA, sur la période 2018-2025, fondée sur une approche mixte à dominante qualitative : analyse des rapports et des lettres de contrôle interne du commissaire aux comptes, questionnaire administré à trente répondants et entretiens semi-directifs, rapprochés par triangulation. La recherche adopte un positionnement post-positiviste et un raisonnement hypothético-déductif. Les biais liés à l’appartenance de l’auteur au cabinet étudié sont analysés de manière systématique ; une analyse de sensibilité écarte notamment l’effet de l’auto-évaluation des répondants du cabinet. Les résultats confirment H1 : le non-respect des procédures est détecté et révélé par écrit sur cinq exercices documentés (93,33 % d’avis favorables pour la détection, 86,67 % pour la révélation). H2 n’est que partiellement confirmée : les recommandations sont formulées (96,67 %) et suivies (70 %, borne basse de 55 % chez les seuls audités), mais ce suivi reste formel : sur cinq exercices documentés, l’observation relative aux marchés publics n’a jamais été levée, et la seule mesure prise, la création d’une cellule de passation des marchés, n’a permis de valider que neuf marchés entre 2022 et 2025, faute de mécanisme d’application au niveau des organes de gouvernance. L’article propose de distinguer la qualité de l’audit de son effectivité et formule des recommandations à l’intention du comité d’audit, de la direction et du commissaire aux comptes. Mots clés : Audit légal ; qualité de l’audit ; commissaire aux comptes ; marchés publics ; recommandations d’audit ; gouvernance ; entreprise publique ; OHADA ; RDC. Abstract This article examines the extent to which statutory audit brings to light non-compliance with public procurement procedures and regulates the behaviour of the actors involved, in a state-owned enterprise of the OHADA zone. Building on De Angelo’s (1981) definition of audit quality, agency theory and corporate governance research, it tests two hypotheses: (H1) audit quality, understood as the auditor’s ability to detect and report irregularities, reveals non-compliance with procurement procedures; (H2) the statutory auditor’s recommendations and their follow-up regulate the behaviour of procurement actors. Adopting a post-positivist stance and hypothetico-deductive reasoning, the study focuses on a single case, GECAMINES SA, over the 2018–2025 period. It relies on a convergent mixed-methods design with a qualitative emphasis, triangulating the auditor’s reports and management letters, a questionnaire administered to thirty respondents and semi-structured interviews. Biases arising from the author’s position within the audit firm are examined systematically, and a sensitivity analysis rules out the effect of self-assessment by audit-firm respondents. The findings support H1: non-compliance is detected and reported in writing over five documented financial years (93.33% favourable responses for detection and 86.67% for reporting). H2 is only partially supported. Recommendations are issued (96.67%) and followed up (70%, with a lower bound of 55% among auditee respondents), but this follow-up remains largely formal: the procurement finding was never cleared over the five documented years, and the only corrective measure, the creation of a procurement unit, led to the validation of just nine contracts between 2022 and 2025. This outcome reflects the absence of an enforcement mechanism within governance bodies. The article therefore distinguishes audit quality from audit effectiveness and offers recommendations to the audit committee, senior management and the statutory auditor. Keywords: Statutory audit; audit quality; statutory auditor; public procurement; audit recommendations; corporate governance; state-owned enterprise; OHADA; DR Congo.

title: Entrepreneurship, Start-ups, MSME, Innovation, Ecosystem and New- Age Business Models; Emerging Trends and Opportunities In India
summary: Entrepreneurship, start-ups and micro, small and Medium Enterprise (MSMEs) have emerged as important components of economic development, employment generation and innovation. The rapid development of digital technologies, artificial intelligence, fintech, e-commerce, social media platforms and cloud-based service has significantly transformed the manner in which businesses are created, operated and scaled. At the same time, the emergence of new-age business models such as platform businesses, subscription models, direct to consumer models, sharing-economy models, digital marketplaces and technology enabled service models has created new opportunities for entrepreneur and MSME. This paper examine the interrelationship between entrepreneurship, startups, MSME, innovation ecosystem and new-age business models in the contemporary Indian business environment. The study adopt a conceptual and descriptive research approach based on secondary source, including academic literature, Government report and institutional publication. The paper identifies major factors influencing entrepreneurial capabilities, incubation, mentoring, market access, networking and government support.

title: The silent shareholder: understanding the governance gap in India’s retail investing boom
summary: Retail investors have long been viewed as passive participants in corporate governance due to the collective action problem, rational apathy and informational disadvantages. However, digital voting, social media, and technology-enabled market access have challenged such age-old justifications. India, a jurisdiction persistently characterised by concentrated ownership, is currently witnessing an unprecedented rise in its retail participation in the securities market. In this context, the paper examines whether the quantitative rise in retail ownership in India is translating into meaningful governance participation. Using empirical data on shareholder voting in selected listed companies, the study finds that despite enhanced regulatory support and digital facilitation, retail shareholders’ voting participation remains critically low and largely mechanical, with a heavy pro-management stance. The paper, therefore, proposes reform-oriented solutions to foster a culture of active participation among retail investors, without which India’s retail investing boom may expand financial inclusion but will remain ineffective from a corporate governance standpoint.

title: КРЕДИТУВАННЯ МАЛОГО ТА СЕРЕДНЬОГО БІЗНЕСУ В УКРАЇНІ: ПРОБЛЕМИ, МОЖЛИВОСТІ ТА ПЕРСПЕКТИВИ РОЗВИТКУ
summary: У статті досліджено трансформацію банківського сектору під впливом цифровізації та обґрунтовано екосистемний підхід як перспективну модель розвитку фінансових установ. Актуальність зумовлена поширенням цифрових технологій, посиленням конкуренції між банками, FinTech-компаніями й цифровими платформами, зміною поведінки споживачів та необхідністю підвищення стійкості банківської системи України в умовах воєнних і макроекономічних викликів. Розглянуто цифровізацію як комплексну трансформацію бізнес-моделей, управління даними, ризик-менеджменту та взаємодії з клієнтами й партнерами, з акцентом на штучний інтелект, Big Data, блокчейн, FinTech та Open Banking. Обґрунтовано перехід від продуктової до екосистемної моделі, що інтегрує фінансові й нефінансові послуги. Визначено її переваги та ризики, пов’язані з кібербезпекою, захистом даних, технологічною залежністю й регуляторними обмеженнями. Окреслено напрями розвитку екосистем в Україні та доведено їх потенціал для підвищення конкурентоспроможності, інноваційності й фінансової стійкості банківського сектору.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Accounting Performance: Examining Accounting Efficiency, Financial Reporting Quality and Managerial Decision-Making
summary: The rapid adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is transforming accounting practices by influencing how financial information is processed, reported, and used for managerial decision-making. However, limited empirical evidence explains how GenAI adoption and accounting efficiency jointly contribute to accounting performance, particularly through financial reporting quality. This study therefore examines the relationships among Generative Artificial Intelligence Adoption, Accounting Efficiency, Financial Reporting Quality, and Accounting Performance within an integrated accounting framework. The study employed a quantitative, cross-sectional approach using data collected from 250 accounting and finance professionals. The relationships among the constructs were examined using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The findings indicate that Generative AI Adoption has a positive effect on Accounting Performance and Financial Reporting Quality, while Accounting Efficiency also has positive effects on both outcomes. Financial Reporting Quality demonstrates a strong positive effect on Accounting Performance and further serves as an important mediating mechanism between Generative AI Adoption and Accounting Performance, as well as between Accounting Efficiency and Accounting Performance. The structural model indicates that the proposed relationships provide meaningful explanatory and predictive value for the endogenous constructs. Overall, the findings suggest that the benefits of Generative AI in accounting extend beyond automation and become more meaningful when AI adoption is supported by efficient accounting processes and high-quality financial reporting. The study contributes to the emerging literature on AI and accounting by providing an integrated perspective on how technological adoption, accounting efficiency, and financial reporting quality can collectively strengthen accounting performance and support managerial decision-making.

title: Water‐Conscious Governance: The Role of Co‐Opted Members in Water Withdrawal
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates the impact of co‐opted board directors on water withdrawal. Based on a U.S. sample of 4194 firm‐year observations between 2008 and 2022, we find that the presence, independence and tenure of co‐opted directors reduce firm water withdrawals. Co‐opted directors can play a constructive role in improving corporate water management by aligning with the CEO environmental initiatives, responding to legitimacy pressures, and supporting strategies that balance profit with stakeholder concerns. Additional analyses reveal that this relationship is stronger when the CEO and board chair roles are separated and in firms with strong corporate governance and environmental performance, as well as in firms that link executive compensation to CSR performance. Also, we show that the effect is prevalent in firms with CSR and nomination committees. Our findings offer new insights for regulators and managers seeking to address water management issues and encourage firms to improve their board structure by increasing board co‐option to better align board decisions with CEO water management policies.

title: Trade Wars on the Income Statement: The Effects of Tariffs on Firms
summary: We study the firm-level effects of the 2018 and 2025 US tariff episodes. Combining bill-of-lading, supply chain, and financial data, we construct exposure measures across three channels: direct import costs, upstream suppliers' costs, and retaliatory tariffs on exports, validated using stock returns and earnings calls. We provide new evidence that, in 2025, cost exposure reduced sales and variable costs by about 1 percentage point for firms with average tariff exposure, with no margin or investment effects, consistent with demand-driven contractions under constant markups.

title: A Multi-Level Grey Evaluation of the Eco-industrial Development Level of Industrial Parks Based on a Combination of Coefficient of Variation and AHM Weighting
summary: To support environmental management and differentiated green transformation in industrial parks, this study develops an evaluation framework that assesses eco-industrial development performance and identifies park-specific strengths and weaknesses. The framework contains 39 indicators across economic development, ecological environment, material circulation, resource potential, technological innovation, and policy and management. Weights are derived using the Attribute Hierarchical Model (AHM) and coefficient of variation method, integrated via the minimum-deviation principle, and applied through multi-level grey evaluation to four Chinese parks. Findings show that policy and management is weighted highest, followed by economic development and ecological environment; overall performance ranks Tianjin, Suzhou, Dalian, and Fushun. Critically, similar aggregate performance masks distinct weaknesses in environmental governance, resource circulation, technological innovation, and resource conditions. The framework therefore enables diagnosis of differentiated management priorities and supports park-specific pathways toward eco-industrial development.

title: Lean Supply Chain 4.0: An Integrative Literature Review of Digital Technologies, Supply Chain Coordination, and Operational Performance
summary: Abstract - With increasingly complex production systems there is an increased need for efficient, flexible, coordinated and sustainable supply chains. Lean manufacturing techniques and Lean Six Sigma (LSS) have been developed to reduce waste, variability and improve quality. Industry 4.0 techniques such as IoT, AI, Big Data, Digital Twins, Blockchain and Cyber Physical Systems provide new opportunities to monitor, predict, automate and share information using digital technologies. Despite having similar aims in improving processes, there are challenges to combine Lean techniques with Industry 4.0 techniques within supply chain networks due to differences in technology, organisational barriers, lack of skills and a lack of a framework that can be applied universally. This paper provides an integrative literature review that focuses on literature related to SCM, Lean and Lean Six Sigma, Industry 4.0, digital transformation and supply chain coordination. The literature has been split into themes so that key findings can be identified. Relationships between research areas have also been identified along with gaps in the literature. The synthesis shows that digital technologies can be used to improve Lean within processes. However, digital technologies do not automatically improve supply chain performance. It depends on how well digital technologies are aligned with process maturity, organisational preparedness, information sharing and continual improvement. A key gap in the research was found to be the absence of an integrated framework that can explain how digital technologies and Lean/Lean Six Sigma can be combined with supply chain coordination to improve operational performance, resilience and sustainability. A conceptual research framework has been proposed along with suggestions for future empirical and modelling research.
