title: Intelligent Decision Support Systems in Investment Planning for Post-War Economic Reconstruction: The Case of Ukraine
summary: Purpose: The article is aimed at investigating the factors of investment planning in the process of post-war reconstruction of Ukraine’s economy and evaluating the basis for the use of intelligent decision support systems in the strategic management of investment activities. Design/Methodology/Approach: Economic and mathematical methodologies, including regression modelling, correlation analysis, and statistical analysis, were implemented. The empirical base was formed using Ukraine’s macroeconomic indicators for 2016–2026, characterising economic growth, investment activity, macroeconomic stability, and the development of the digital economy. Several econometric models were built to assess the impact of investment factors on economic growth. Research Limitation: The study is based on 11 annual observations (2016–2026, partly projected) of Ukraine’s macroeconomic indicators and provides a basis for further research on investment planning during post-war reconstruction. Findings: Macroeconomic and investment indicators alone did not significantly explain the dynamics of economic growth (R² = 0.423), while the model including institutional and structural indicators achieved R² = 0.995, with industrial production and foreign direct investment as significant factors. The share of Information and Communication Technology services exports increased from 18.56% in 2016 to 53.18% in 2026, indicating the growing role of the digital economy in post-war recovery. Practical Implication: Intelligent decision support systems can support strategic investment management by predicting investment outcomes, identifying reconstruction priorities, and forming optimal investment portfolios. Social Implication: More effective investment planning can contribute to sustainable post-war economic recovery. Originality/Value: The study substantiates the use of intelligent decision support systems as a basis for strategic investment management in Ukraine’s post-war reconstruction.

title: PENGARUH MEDIASI GREEN INNOVATION TERHADAP SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT DAN TRIPLE BOTTOM LINE PERFORMANCE: STUDI UMKM DAERAH ISTIMEWA YOGYAKARTA
summary: Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah (UMKM) memiliki peran penting dalam pembangunan ekonomi, tetapi integrasi prinsip keberlanjutan lingkungan dan sosial ke dalam aktivitas bisnis masih menjadi tantangan, khususnya di negara berkembang. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Sustainable Supply Chain Management (SCM) terhadap Green Innovation (GI) dan Triple Bottom Line (TBL) Performance, serta menguji peran mediasi Green Innovation dalam hubungan antara SCM dan TBL Performance. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain eksplanatori. Data primer dikumpulkan melalui penyebaran kuesioner terstruktur kepada pemilik atau pengelola UMKM sektor industri kreatif di Daerah Istimewa Yogyakarta, Indonesia data dikumpulkan pada tahun 2026. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan metode Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan bantuan perangkat lunak SmartPLS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa SCM berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Green Innovation (T-statistics = 15,135; p < 0,001) dan TBL Performance (T-statistics = 6,931; p < 0,001). Selanjutnya, Green Innovation terbukti berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap TBL Performance (T-statistics = 2,431; p = 0,015). Hasil pengujian pengaruh tidak langsung juga menunjukkan bahwa Green Innovation secara signifikan memediasi hubungan antara SCM dan TBL Performance (T-statistics = 2,412; p = 0,016). Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa pengelolaan rantai pasok yang efektif tidak hanya meningkatkan efisiensi operasional, tetapi juga mendorong inovasi berorientasi lingkungan yang pada akhirnya memperkuat kinerja ekonomi, sosial, dan lingkungan UMKM. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi terhadap literatur keberlanjutan dengan menegaskan pentingnya Green Innovation sebagai mekanisme strategis dalam mentransformasikan efisiensi rantai pasok menjadi kinerja keberlanjutan yang komprehensif.

title: Design And Development Of A Web-Based Digital Credit Service And Qris Transaction System
summary: The rapid development of financial technology (fintech) has accelerated the adoption of digital payment and digital credit services. However, most digital credit services still rely on cash disbursement mechanisms, making it difficult to control the utilization of borrowed funds. This study aims to develop PayQRIS, a web-based Buy Now, Pay Later (PayLater) service integrated with QRIS payments that enables cashless transactions using credit limits without direct cash disbursement. The system was developed using the Prototyping model and evaluated through black-box testing and the System Usability Scale (SUS). The results show that PayQRIS successfully integrates PayLater services with QRIS payments into a single platform featuring credit limit determination, installment and bill management, bill extension, and secure transaction authentication. Functional testing confirmed that all system features operated according to the specified requirements, while the usability evaluation produced a SUS score of 83.25, indicating a high level of usability and user acceptance. Therefore, PayQRIS provides a web-based PayLater solution that supports QRIS payments through a more controlled digital credit mechanism.

title: Machine Learning Meets Blockchain: A Domain-Oriented Review of Integration Mechanisms, Applications and Open Challenges
summary: Blockchain and machine learning (ML) are combined in systems that must learn from multi-party data and keep a verifiable record of what was used and decided. This scoping-style review of a ranked sample covers seven domains: healthcare, finance, supply chain, energy, smart contracts, transportation and education. We searched Scopus and IEEE Xplore on 15 October 2026, ranked 5,195 candidate records, read 345 abstracts in rank order, coded a core corpus of 192 studies and read 38 in full. Federated learning is the most common method (93 of 192 core studies name it), and detection of fraud, intrusions and vulnerabilities is the most common task among the 38. None of the 38 reports a deployment, 24 report a measured ledger figure and two measure ledger energy. Ten use more than one privacy mechanism, and only two report accuracy with and without it. Attack tests are small, and one study tests a Sybil attacker. Studies differ too much to compare, so we do not rank domains. A ledger shows that a record has not changed, not that it was correct when written. The main gaps are realistic evaluation, shared benchmarks and reporting standards, and tested explanations for decisions made inside contracts.

title: The Effect of Financial Reporting Transparency on Audit Report Quality in Kenyan Public Universities
summary: This study examined the effect of financial reporting transparency on audit report quality in Kenyan public universities. The quality of audit reports in Kenyan public universities remains a concern due to inadequate financial disclosures, incomplete reporting, and limited accessibility of financial information, which undermine audit reliability and institutional accountability. Anchored on Agency Theory, the study adopted a positivist research philosophy and a cross-sectional research design. The target population comprised 175 respondents, representing five respondents from each of the 35 publicly chartered universities, including finance officers, internal auditors, accountants, and audit or finance committee members. Institutional census and purposive sampling techniques were employed. Four universities outside the target population participated in the pilot study. Primary data were collected using structured questionnaires, while secondary data were obtained from published audit reports and financial statements. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression. Findings indicated moderately high financial reporting transparency (M = 3.63, SD = 1.24) and a positive, statistically significant relationship with audit report quality (r = 0.612, p < 0.01; ? = 0.598, p < 0.05), explaining 37.5 per cent of its variation (R² = 0.375). The study concluded that transparent financial reporting facilitates reliable audit assessments by ensuring the availability of complete, timely, and accessible financial information. It recommends strengthening disclosure requirements and financial reporting practices to enhance audit credibility. The findings provide evidence to inform financial reporting policies, strengthen institutional oversight, and promote accountability in Kenyan public universities.

title: From innovation to accountability: Governing AI in public administration
summary: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in public administration, creating new challenges involving accountability, transparency, explainability, and workforce preparedness. Although state governments are developing AI governance frameworks, it remains unclear whether accountability principles are translated into practical mechanisms for governing AI use. Objective This study examines how state AI governance policies operationalize accountability in public administration and identifies remaining gaps in responsibility, oversight, and enforceability. Methods A qualitative comparative policy analysis was conducted using publicly available AI governance frameworks from 24 U.S. states identified through March 2026. The documents were analyzed using thematic categories addressing accountability and related governance mechanisms, including transparency, human oversight, auditing, risk management, training, documentation, public notice, appeals, and enforcement. The study distinguished between symbolic accountability, in which accountability is expressed primarily as a governance principle, and operational accountability, in which policies establish identifiable mechanisms for implementation and oversight. Results Eighteen of the 24 states explicitly identified accountability as an AI governance principle. However, accountability was frequently expressed symbolically rather than through operational mechanisms. State frameworks more consistently addressed principles such as transparency and risk management while providing less direction regarding enforcement, appeals, independent review, documentation, monitoring, and responsibility for harmful AI-assisted outcomes. Conclusions State governments increasingly recognize accountability as an important component of AI governance, but mechanisms for putting accountability into practice remain uneven. Effective public-sector AI governance requires clearer responsibility structures, human oversight, documentation, auditability, review and appeal procedures, and workforce preparation. Without these mechanisms, accountability may remain largely symbolic and responsibility may be shifted toward public-sector workers who are expected to use and justify AI-assisted decisions.

title: Digitalization as a tool for developing the state’s social responsibility in the sphere of social protection in wartime conditions and post-war reconstruction
summary: The article clarifies the theoretical foundations and develops approaches to the digital transformation of the social protection system in the context of developing the state’s social responsibility in wartime. The study used logical analysis and generalization, grouping, comparison, and relative quantities. The study considered the role and impact of digitalization of the social sphere on the development of the state’s social responsibility. The study substantiated the feasibility of digitalization in social protection in the context of wartime challenges. The study analyzed statistical indicators and characteristics of digitalization in Ukraine’s social protection system. The study systematized the features of digitalization in the social sphere during wartime. The study outlined the problems of using digital solutions in Ukraine’s social protection system. The study systematized the advantages and obstacles to digitalization in social protection. The study further developed the justification for the drivers of digital transformation in the social protection system in the context of the development of the state’s social responsibility. A model for further digital transformation of the social protection system in the context of the development of the state’s social responsibility and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals, which involves the transformation of the state’s social responsibility from reactive and compensatory to proactive, integrated and socially adaptive, with a combination of the military and post-war contours of its development. The proposed model is based on the interconnected development of digital data integration, proactivity, targeting, digital inclusion, cybersecurity, sustainability, and people-centeredness of the social protection system. Future research in this area should develop a mechanism for the digital transformation of the social protection system. title: Data privacy and audit compliance of supply chain finance warehouse receipt pledge based on WSN federated edge learning
summary: Abstract In supply chain finance warehouse receipt pledge financing, the status of the pledged assets is difficult to verify in real time, the risk of privacy leakage of financing data is high, and the federal training process lacks verifiable audit trajectories for regulatory authorities. To achieve multi-warehouse collaborative risk control modeling under the condition of data not leaving the domain and meet the requirements of privacy protection and audit compliance, a method for privacy and audit compliance of supply chain finance warehouse receipt pledge data based on federated edge learning of wireless sensor networks is constructed. A pledge perception and digital warehouse receipt generation mechanism based on wireless sensor networks is designed. A federated edge learning architecture integrating trust and energy-aware weighted aggregation, federated proximal terms and communication compression is constructed. The study introduces a joint security aggregation mechanism of differential privacy and homomorphic encryption, as well as an audit compliance framework for blockchain smart contracts. The experimental results show that when the data heterogeneity parameter is 0.1, the test accuracy of the proposed method reaches 88.4%, which is 9.9% higher than the 78.5% of the federal average algorithm. In the ablation experiment, the F1 score of the complete method is 93.6%, while it drops to 88.9% after removing the federal proximal term. When the privacy budget is 0.10, the accuracy rate of the proposed method is 92.1%, which is 8.0% higher than the 84.1% of the federal average algorithm. The results show that the proposed method has stronger robustness under extreme non-independent homogeneous distribution conditions. Trust and energy-aware selection and federated proximal terms contribute significantly to accuracy, and the privacy enhancement mechanism achieves effective privacy protection with limited accuracy loss. This research provides a technical path that takes into account data privacy, model performance and audit compliance for the warehouse receipt pledge scenario in supply chain finance, which is conducive to promoting the compliant application of federated learning in supply chain finance risk control.

title: Patient Capital, Accounting Information Disclosure Quality, and the Cost of Debt Financing
summary: This paper examines whether patient capital is associated with lower debt financing costs and whether accounting information disclosure quality strengthens this association. Using 23,124 firm-year observations of non-financial Chinese A-share listed firms from 2012 to 2024, we construct a multidimensional patient-capital index combining investor horizon, institutional ownership stability, short-term financing pressure, equity growth retention, and managerial short-termism measured from MD&A text. The cost of debt is proxied by financial expenses divided by total liabilities. Two-way fixed-effects estimates show a negative association between patient capital and debt financing costs, and the result remains stable across alternative variable definitions, lagged specifications, sample exclusions, and supplementary 2SLS and GMM estimations. Channel tests are consistent with three potential pathways: stronger market power, lower operating cost ratios, and lower financial risk. Using stock-exchange disclosure ratings, we find a negative and significant interaction between patient capital and disclosure quality, indicating that higher-quality disclosure strengthens the negative association between patient capital and debt costs. Subsample estimates are statistically significant only for eastern-region, technology-intensive, profitable, and smaller firms. The findings suggest that long-horizon capital and credible disclosure can operate as complementary signals in creditor assessment: patient capital conveys a long-term orientation, while higher-quality disclosure improves the verifiability of that signal.

title: A Discussion On Ecological Coexistence Under Epistemic Limits in Future Urban Design
summary: Ecological coexistence becomes an ethical and institutional problem when an intervention changes the opportunities through which different lives and ecological relations may persist, recover, or develop. Infrastructure provides important services while transforming habitats and shifting environmental burdens across places and generations. Evaluation therefore faces a connected difficulty: ecological interests may diverge across biological scales, while the knowledge and authority required to respond often develop after change is underway. This paper develops possibility-sensitive ecological evaluation as a relational framework for examining these conditions. It distinguishes the continued viability of ecological pathways from the capacity to observe and understand them, treating future knowability as a consideration alongside organismal welfare and ecological recovery. Historical dependence, political representation, and successor stewardship enter the analysis because interventions can transform both ecological circumstances and the evidence available for later judgment. The Elwha River dam removals provide a documentary study of sediment disturbance, uneven biological recovery, Tribal stewardship, and adaptive management. Historical forecasts, monitoring records, and retrospective models are assessed according to what they establish about decisions and outcomes; the unchosen September 2013 delay remains a counterfactual requiring further reconstruction. A hypothetical comparison of AI-oriented urban infrastructure then considers how equivalent computing services can distribute resource use and ecological exposure across facilities and supply chains. The resulting evaluative procedure connects feasible alternatives and affected ecological relations to decision-time evidence, authority to intervene, protective response windows, and continuing responsibility. The paper offers a conceptual and documentary contribution, with causal tests and project-specific comparisons identified as future empirical work.

title: U.S.-CHINA RIVALRY OVER CRITICAL MINERALS: STRATEGIC IMPLICATIONS FOR GEOPOLITICS, SUPPLY CHAINS, AND TECHNOLOGICAL DOMINANCE
summary: Critical minerals have become a central arena of U.S.–China strategic competition because they underpin advanced semiconductors, electric vehicles, renewable energy, aerospace and defense technologies. China’s advantage is not limited to its access to mineral resources; its extensive control over processing, refining, manufacturing, infrastructure and supply-chain networks creates significant vulnerabilities for the United States and its allies. This paper examines how Washington and Beijing are competing to secure critical-mineral supply chains and how efforts to reduce strategic dependence can generate reciprocal threat perceptions and deepen geopolitical rivalry. It examines three strategically important resource regions— the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ukraine, and Greenland—to assess how resource endowments, political instability, infrastructure, foreign investment, and strategic partnerships are shaping the competition. The analysis argues that complete decoupling from China is neither immediately feasible nor strategically desirable. Instead, the United States should pursue supply-chain resilience through domestic mining and refining, strategic stockpiling, recycling and technological innovation, cooperation with trusted allies and deeper engagement with resource-rich states. The paper concludes that critical minerals are increasingly instruments of economic statecraft and geopolitical leverage, and that competition over their supply chains will play an important role in determining the future distribution of technological, economic, and strategic power.

title: Library Digitization Practices and their Impact on Services: The Case of Hei Libraries in Region XII
summary: This study explores library digitization and their impact on services in private academic libraries in Region XII, Philippines. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, it examines librarians’ experiences regarding the reasons, benefits, impacts, and challenges of digital transformation. Findings reveal that digitization enhances resource preservation, accessibility, service modernization, and operational efficiency. It also improves user satisfaction, efficiency, and resource sharing while strengthening Library services through faster retrieval and remote access. However, challenges such as budget constraints, technological limitations, resistance to adaptation, workload pressures, and limited dissemination persist. Despite these issues, librarians view digitization as essential to sustainable, user-centered library services. The study is anchored on Digital Transformation Framework, Technology Acceptance Model 3 (TAM3) and, Sociotechnical Systems Theory emphasizing libraries’ evolving role in knowledge access and innovation.

title: Electronic Human Resources Management and Its Role in Improving the Performance of Health Organizations in Zintan City
summary: This study aimed to identify the current reality of electronic human resources management (e-HRM) and its role in improving the performance of health organizations in zintan city. The study adopted a descriptive analytical approach and applied a questionnaire to a stratified random sample of (152) employees working in health organizations in zintan. The findings confirmed the acceptance of the general hypothesis that e-HRM, with its human and technical requirements and elements, plays a positive role in improving human resources performance. However, the results also revealed a clear weakness in the technical infrastructure, an absence of active digital transformation projects, and shortcomings in implementing electronic HR activities particularly in career planning and e-training along with a deficiency in motivating employees to acquire technological skills. The study recommended developing a clear strategic plan for digital transformation, upgrading infrastructure, training human cadres, and fostering a culture of digital innovation to ensure enhanced healthcare service quality.

title: The Moderating Role of Accounting Conservatism in the Relationship Between ESG Disclosure and Company Value: Evidence from Korea and China
summary: This study examines ESG disclosure’s effect on company value and accounting conservatism’s moderating role. Using Korean and Chinese listed firms for out‑of‑sample validation, we find that ESG disclosure positively affects company value, which is more pronounced when financial reporting is less conservative. Results hold under 2SLS and T+1 tests. It suggests that ESG disclosure not only serves as a direct value-enhancing signal but also functions as a complementary mechanism substituting for conservatism. It indicates that increasing ESG disclosure can serve as a strategic communication tool to enhance firm valuation, offering insights for the coordination of financial and non-financial disclosure regulations.

title: KETIDAKSEIMBANGAN HUMAN, MACHINE, ORGANIZATION SEBAGAI TANTANGAN TATA KELOLA DIGITAL DESA: STUDI KASUS DESA MALATIRO, KABUPATEN MAMASA
summary: The rapid development of digital technology has transformed governance practices, including at the local level. However, the implementation of digital governance in rural contexts remains uneven, primarily due to limitations in human resource capacity, technological infrastructure, and institutional readiness. This study aims to analyze the integration of human, machine, and organization dimensions in realizing digital governance in Malatiro Village. The study employs a qualitative case study approach, with data collection techniques including in-depth interviews, observations, and document analysis involving village officials, community members, and relevant stakeholders. Data were analyzed using an interactive analysis model and interpreted through the human–machine–organization framework. The findings indicate that the implementation of digital governance in Malatiro Village is still at an early stage of digitalization and is characterized by structural misalignment among the three dimensions. In the human dimension, limited digital literacy, low technical capacity, and rigid mental and emotional responses constitute the main barriers to digital system adoption. In the machine dimension, infrastructure limitations, unstable internet connectivity, and suboptimal utilization of information systems hinder technology from functioning effectively as an enabler. Meanwhile, in the organization dimension, the absence of strategic policies, weak institutional structures, and limited leadership commitment impede the sustainability of digital transformation. This study contributes to the literature on digital governance by demonstrating that successful digital transformation at the village level critically depends on a balanced integration of human capacity, technological readiness, and organizational support. In addition, it highlights the importance of psychological and cultural factors in influencing technology adoption, which are often overlooked in previous studies. Practically, these findings emphasize the need for a holistic and integrative strategy to strengthen digital governance in rural areas. Keywords: digital governance; human–machine–organization; digital transformation; village governance; capacity building

title: Designing the future: How will informatics education in secondary schools change with the introduction of the new standard
summary: The change in technological structure, characterized by the rapid development of artificial intelligence, big data technologies and increasing demands on the technological sovereignty of the country, necessitates a review of approaches to the training of high school graduates. Informatics, as a subject that forms digital literacy, algorithmic and computational thinking, is designed to ensure that the younger generation is ready for life and professional activity in the digital economy. The Draft Federal State Educational Standard for Secondary General Education for 2026 offers a significantly updated content of the subject "Informatics" that meets modern challenges.Based on a comparative analysis of the draft standard on the subject of "Informatics" at the basic and advanced levels with the current standard, new substantive lines have been identified: artificial intelligence, simulation modeling, data engineering, system administration. Special attention is paid to the methodological aspects of the implementation of new content in high school. Specific practice-oriented approaches to the formation of students' understanding of the role of big data, skills in working with search engines and the basics of simulation modeling are proposed.

title: PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AS AN ELEMENT OF NATIONAL SUSTAINABILITY IN A CHANGING GEOPOLITICAL ENVIRONMENT
summary: The article examines the role of public administration as a key determinant of national resilience in the context of a rapidly changing geopolitical environment. The analysis focuses on contemporary security challenges such as armed conflicts, hybrid threats, cyber risks, energy insecurity, and disinformation campaigns. A conceptual framework is developed, linking public administration capacity with national resilience and security. The study highlights the increasing importance of institutional coordination, crisis management capacity, digital transformation, and strategic communication. The findings confirm that public administration is not only an implementing mechanism of state policies but also a central pillar of resilience and national security in conditions of systemic uncertainty.

title: An Integrated Indicator-Weight Evolution Method for Sustainable Industrial Supply Chains in Dynamic Scenarios
summary: The resilience and stability of industrial supply chains are the core pillars of the sustainable development of the global economy, and also an important foundation for achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals of “Responsible Consumption and Production” and “Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure”. To address the problem that traditional industrial supply chain risk assessment systems have fixed indicators and static weights, which are difficult to adapt to complex scenarios such as dynamic adjustments of supply chain nodes, fluctuations in market demand and changes in geopolitical patterns, and thus restrict the construction of sustainable supply chain resilience, this paper proposes a comprehensive indicator-weight dynamic evolution algorithm for industrial supply chain risk assessment systems. Firstly, the evolutionary characteristics and trigger rules of the industrial supply chain risk system are defined. Indicator-weight evolution is performed when the original indicator system can no longer meet the evaluation requirements. The Delphi method combined with the actual risk characteristics of the supply chain is adopted to determine the candidate indicator set. The candidate indicators are screened using the grey relational analysis algorithm and the entropy weight-variation coefficient method to construct the evolved risk indicator set. Secondly, an improved DEMATEL model is used to analyze the causal relationships among the evolved indicators. Evolutionary analysis of the original indicator weights is carried out according to the influence degrees between indicators, so as to obtain the evolved indicator weights and realize the dynamic linkage update of evaluation weights. This study conducts a case analysis using publicly available aggregated synthetic data on supply chain disruptions and resilience and compares the proposed method with the entropy weight–analytic hierarchy process (EW-AHP) and dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) methods. The performance of the methods is evaluated in terms of the consistency of indicator weights or relative importance, computational time, out-of-sample prediction performance, and retrospective analysis of a representative disruption event scenario. The results indicate that, under the current case and parameter settings, the proposed method can reconstruct the risk indicator system and coordinate indicator and weight updates, demonstrating certain advantages in computational efficiency and risk factor identification in the specified comparative experiments. It should be noted, however, that the current validation relies primarily on publicly available synthetic aggregated data and retrospective event-scenario analysis. Therefore, the evidence is insufficient to directly establish the risk-warning benefits or improvements in operational response efficiency that the method might deliver in real-world enterprise settings. This study provides a methodological framework for the coordinated updating of indicators and weights in dynamic industrial supply chain risk assessment. Its applicability across industries and practical effectiveness require further validation using independent data sources and actual enterprise operational data.

title: Computing Power Deployment and Enterprise Innovation Resilience: A Dynamic Capability Perspective
summary: In the digital era, computing power deployment has emerged as a strategic resource for building enterprise innovation resilience; however, the mechanisms through which it exerts such effects remain unclear. Drawing on dynamic capability theory, this study examines how computing power deployment influences enterprise innovation resilience using a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2012 to 2024. The results indicate that computing power deployment significantly enhances enterprise innovation resilience, and this finding holds after a series of robustness checks. Mechanism analysis shows that computing power deployment exerts its effects through two pathways: technology diversification, which strengthens knowledge recombination and trajectory switching capabilities, and organizational inertia, which ensures innovation process continuity and frees cognitive resources for higher-order reconfiguration. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the effect is stronger among state-owned enterprises, large firms, firms in strategic emerging industries, and firms with high patient capital, reflecting four boundary conditions: resource foundation, organizational carrier, environmental fit, and temporal support. This study extends the antecedent research on innovation resilience by introducing the computing power perspective, reveals the transformation mechanisms and boundary conditions of computing power deployment, and provides implications for innovation resilience building and computing power resource allocation in the digital economy.

title: Scaling vs. Transforming Climate Finance
summary: This article examines how climate finance can address three longstanding gaps: the lack of integration of science into action, the inequities associated with the adoption of novel technologies, and the lack of voice for individuals with lived experience. Using a comparative qualitative case study of the European Union’s (EU) Green Bond Framework and the South African Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP), this article examines how finance is carried out differently, depending on the circumstances of the developed/developing worlds. The EU example illustrates a high level of scientific integration, in the form of taxonomies, as a mechanism for scaling technology, but exposes the drawback of technocratic isolation. On the other hand, JETP in South Africa demonstrates that finance can be a transformative process that incorporates justice and community involvement, including indigenous knowledge, despite obstacles such as weak governance and structural injustices. Informed by the sustainable development goals (SDGs), the theory of planned behavior, and climate justice principles, this article finds that climate finance needs to focus on both scientific precision and social fairness, as well as on the inclusive scaling of technology and the integration of distributive, procedural, and recognitional justice to act as a transformative vehicle between knowledge and action.

title: A Method-Derived Framework for Evidence-Based Sustainability Reporting Education: Environmental Materiality, ESG Literacy and Colombian Manufacturing
summary: This study examines how corporate sustainability reports and official environmental statistics can be combined analytically to support a conceptual framework for sustainability education, ESG literacy, environmental accounting, and professional training in business, management, and engineering programs. Focusing on Colombian manufacturing, the study triangulates GRI-coded corporate disclosures with sector-level indicators on waste generation, water use, and environmental investment. The findings identify strong structural alignment for water-related disclosure, partial alignment for waste and emissions themes, and recurrent emphasis on governance and social topics that are weakly connected to the selected environmental-pressure indicators. On the basis of this analytical sequence, the article proposes a method-derived pedagogical framework for critically comparing sustainability narratives with external evidence. The framework was not tested as an educational intervention: no students, instructors, courses, comparison conditions, or learning outcomes were evaluated. Accordingly, the educational contribution should be interpreted as a conceptually grounded application of the research method rather than evidence of demonstrated teaching effectiveness. title: Artificial Intelligence Changes Cognition Systems
summary: Purpose of the study. Humanity is at a turning point in its development, which is reflected in the change in the regimes of global processes, the growth of global hypercompetition for the future. Digital transformation is also entering a new phase. The processes of automation, digitalization, and the formation of intellectual production are gradually transforming, and technological development is being replaced by socio-technological development. The world changing before our eyes is becoming more complex, knowledge about it goes beyond the set of individual disciplines and continuously develops as innovative digital transformations grow, including the formation of artificial intelligence. The purpose of the article is to formulate humanitarian problems in the implementation of AI technologies in science and to develop possible directions for their solution. Materials and methods. The research was carried out based on a study and a systematic review of the literature, using methods of comparative analysis and typologization, analysis of epistemic risks based on the synthesis of analyzed sources. The use of the conceptual modeling method made it possible to describe the iterative “datamodel-experiment” cycle as the basis of the Fifth paradigm and justify the key role of understanding in this process. Research results: the analysis made it possible to systematize modern ideas about AI scientists, as well as to highlight the fundamental limitations, risks and prospects for their integration into scientific practice. The article, based on the works of foreign researchers, reviewed the key issues of the use of AI in science and the development of AI scientists. The current trends in the development of AI technologies that form the use of artificial intelligence for scientific discoveries are analyzed, the best ways to use AI and the problems associated with them are considered. Key limitations and problems of the “AI-scientist” have been identified. General ideas and practical AI solutions that affect the cognition system are described; fundamental limitations and key problems in the use of AI scientists are reflected. Conclusion. Monitoring new knowledge, identifying, creating and storing key information and data from exponentially growing streams have become impossible without highly developed artificial intelligence. The fourth scientific paradigm actually ended: big data gave way to a cognitive system that organizes an interactive research process an iterative cycle of creating new knowledge. The model created on the basis of data during the experiment provides new data, further analysis of which, supplemented by expert knowledge and elements of interdisciplinary knowledge, allows it to improve and refine the initial hypothesis. Thus, the processes of cognition are continuously accelerated and changed. The study confirms that the world scientific community is at the point of bifurcation associated with the transition from the Fourth paradigm (based on big data and computing) to the Fifth paradigm, in which the central link is the cognitive system that implements the iterative cycle “data model experiment new knowledge”. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLM) act as catalysts for this transition, radically changing the methodology, speed and very nature of scientific search. The authors believe that new approaches and solutions can significantly advance the creation of AI capable of scientific reasoning. However, when working with AI scientists, it is necessary to take into account epistemic risks, as well as the fact that the landscape of AI technologies is changing extremely quickly, which requires constant updating of the obtained typologies and conclusions.

title: Conceptual foundations for forming an organizational-economic mechanism for the development of business structures in the context of digitalization
summary: The article provides a theoretical justification for developing an organizational-economic mechanism for business development in the context of digitalization. The study’s relevance stems from the increasingly dynamic market environment, the widespread adoption of digital technologies, and the need to adapt management systems to new business conditions. The article aims to provide a theoretical justification for the nature, structural and functional design, and principles underlying the development of an organizational and economic mechanism for business development, taking into account the impact of digitalization. The study’s methodological framework draws on systems, structural and functional, and process approaches, along with methods of analysis, synthesis, comparison, systematization, and abstract and logical generalization. The study systematizes academic approaches to defining the concept of an ‘organizational and economic mechanism’ and summarises the main areas of its theoretical interpretation. The article proposes an original definition of an organizational and economic mechanism for business development in the context of digitalization as a purposeful, manageable system of organizational, economic, innovative, and digital forms, methods, levers, and management tools. These are designed to align resources, business processes, and management decisions to improve operational efficiency, adapt to changes in the business environment, facilitate technological renewal, and achieve strategic objectives. The rationale for distinguishing between the organizational, economic, innovative, and digital components of the mechanism is substantiated, and their respective functions are explained. The study establishes that the mechanism’s effectiveness depends on the coordinated interaction of its elements, rational resource use, management adaptability, and appropriate information and analytical support. Digitalization is considered a factor in transforming and improving the mechanism, contributing to the automation of business processes, more timely management decisions, and an enhanced capacity of business organizations to respond to changes in the external environment. The practical significance of the findings lies in their potential to improve business development management systems and develop adaptive business models in the context of digital transformation. Keywords: organizational and economic mechanism, business organizations, digitalization, business development, organizational component, economic levers, innovation, digital technologies, development management, adaptability.

title: Organizational and Economic Aspects of Increasing The Competitiveness of Service Enterprises Mechanisms
summary: The competitive advantage of service enterprises is vital for their success in modern market economies. Effective management of competitiveness through organizational and economic mechanisms is essential in maintaining long-term viability in a rapidly evolving market. This is particularly relevant in Uzbekistan's service sector, where globalization and technological advancements have intensified competition. Service enterprises must leverage strategic management, innovation, and resource optimization to gain and sustain competitive advantages. Although various theories exist on competitive advantage, including Porter's framework and the resource-based approach, a detailed analysis of integrated organizational, economic, and marketing mechanisms tailored to the service industry remains underexplored. This study aims to identify and evaluate the key strategies for enhancing the competitiveness of service enterprises in Uzbekistan. It explores how competitive advantages are formed through cost leadership, differentiation, and specialization strategies, focusing on the service sector's unique characteristics. The research highlights that integrating organizational, economic, and innovative mechanisms leads to sustainable competitive advantage. Key strategies such as cost optimization, service differentiation, and digital transformation were identified as critical factors in strengthening competitiveness. This study offers a comprehensive approach that incorporates modern management theories with industry-specific factors to develop effective competitive strategies for service enterprises. The findings suggest practical recommendations for service enterprises, including the adoption of flexible pricing systems, digital service enhancements, and workforce training. Further research could explore the application of these strategies in different regional contexts.

title: Litigation risk, institutional ownership and corporate greenwashing
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how litigation risk affects corporate greenwashing among Chinese A-share listed non-financial firms from 2009 to 2022. It explores whether firms facing greater legal pressure adopt symbolic environmental, social and governance (ESG) disclosure to preserve legitimacy and manage stakeholder perceptions. The study also investigates whether institutional ownership moderates this relationship and whether the effects differ across ownership structure and audit quality. Design/methodology/approach The analysis uses firm-level panel data regression models with firm, industry and year fixed effects. Multiple robustness tests are conducted to address endogeneity concerns and verify result consistency. The study further performs moderation analysis for institutional ownership and heterogeneity analysis for ownership structure and audit quality. Findings The results show that higher litigation risk significantly increases the likelihood of corporate greenwashing, indicating that legal pressure encourages symbolic rather than substantive ESG practices. Institutional ownership weakens this relationship, highlighting the monitoring role of institutional investors. The positive effect of litigation risk is stronger in non-state-owned enterprises and firms not audited by Big Four accounting firms. These results remain robust across alternative model specifications. Originality/value This study introduces litigation risk as a strategic driver of corporate greenwashing and extends legitimacy theory to the Chinese context. It demonstrates how legal pressure and governance mechanisms jointly shape firms’ ESG disclosure behavior. The findings offer new insights for regulators and investors aiming to strengthen ESG reporting standards, enhance enforcement and promote authentic sustainability practices in emerging markets.

title: Embedding anticipatory science diplomacy in South African higher education governance: A framework for ethical foresight and adaptive leadership
summary: Abstract Public universities in South Africa – and globally – are being asked to do more than teach and produce knowledge. They are expected to steward shared futures amid technological disruption, ecological instability, political volatility, and entrenched social inequality. Yet governance practices often remain procedurally rigid and reactive, shaped by compliance imperatives and inherited administrative logics that assume a more predictable environment than the one universities now inhabit. This paper proposes a Governance Learning and Development Framework that reframes governance as a site of learning – where anticipatory capacity, ethical judgement, and systems awareness can be strengthened through routine decision practices rather than episodic training. Using a theory-adaptation approach, the paper takes the Geneva Science and Diplomacy Anticipator’s (GESDA) Anticipatory Science Diplomacy framework – developed for the multilateral system – and adapts it for the internal governance of universities, reading it through three lenses: Complexity Theory, the King V Code of Corporate Governance, and Heracleous and Lan’s [56] ‘Third Possibility.’ The adaptation yields a four-module learning model – Systems and Complexity Thinking, Ethical Foresight and Legitimacy, Stakeholder Governance, and Futures Literacy and Science Diplomacy – designed to be embedded in ordinary governance rhythms such as agenda-setting, decision papers, and minutes. Illustrative examples from South African innovation contexts are used to show why anticipatory governance matters when universities operate as nodal institutions linking science, society, and diplomacy. The paper argues that governance learning is a practical pathway for universities to ‘thrive together’ by making ethical reasoning, stakeholder legitimacy, and future consequences visible at the point of decision.

title: How STARA-enabled technological readiness shapes intrapreneurial behaviour and digital competence in China's electric vehicle (EV) manufacturing sector
summary: Purpose This study examines how employees' perceptions of STARA (smart technologies, artificial intelligence, robotics, and algorithms) influence their intrapreneurial behaviour (IB) and digital competence (DC), and how digital dynamism (DD) conditions this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, Sociotechnical Systems Theory, and the Antecedents–Decisions–Outcome framework, the study develops an integrated model explaining how employees' perceptions of STARA shape behavioural responses and digital capability development. Data were collected from full-time employees in China's electric vehicle (EV) manufacturing sector, a context characterized by extensive use of STARA technologies, using an online survey and stratified purposive sampling, resulting in 193 valid responses. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was applied to test the proposed model. Findings The results show that positive perceptions of STARA are associated with higher levels of IB and DC. IB serves as a key mechanism through which perceived STARA relates to DC. This highlights the role of employee behaviour in capability development. DD weakens the positive relationship between perceived STARA and DC, suggesting that high environmental turbulence may constrain employees' ability to translate perceived technological opportunities into DC. Research limitations/implications The study offers a socio-technical explanation of digital capability development by showing how employees' interpretations of technological change and their behavioural responses jointly shape capability outcomes. It highlights the importance of aligning technological change with employee-driven adaptation under conditions of environmental uncertainty. Practical implications The findings provide insights for managers in technology-intensive manufacturing firms. They show how employees' perceptions of STARA and intrapreneurial behaviour can contribute to DC. Social implications The findings suggest that fostering IB and DC can enhance employee adaptability, employability, and career resilience, contributing to a more digitally prepared workforce amid ongoing technological transformation. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature on digital transformation and capability development. It integrates employees' perceptions of STARA with employee behaviour within a sociotechnical framework in the EV manufacturing context.

title: Who Answers for the Agent? Agentic AI, Delegated Execution, and Accountability in the Corporate Finance Function
summary: Purpose – Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems can now interpret goals, select software tools and execute financial transactions with limited human involvement. This paper asks how delegating execution authority to such systems affects financial decision quality, risk exposure and accountability in the corporate finance function, and which organizational conditions keep accountability intact. Design/methodology/approach – This is a conceptual, model-building paper. It synthesizes agency theory, management control theory, dynamic capabilities theory and research on human–AI organizing, and draws on supervisory guidance on AI in the financial sector to identify risk categories. Findings – The paper develops the Algorithmic Financial Accountability Framework (AFAF). AFAF distinguishes permission to advise, to decide and to execute. It proposes that agentic autonomy has an inverted-U relationship with decision quality, increases algorithmic risk exposure, and widens an accountability gap between nominal and effective responsibility. Oversight effectiveness, governance maturity, decision irreversibility and third-party concentration condition these effects. Nine propositions are developed. Originality/value – The paper separates the technical locus of action from the organizational locus of accountability. It introduces the autonomy–governance gap as a measurable, dynamic construct and specifies indicators and research designs for testing the framework. Practical implications – Chief financial officers, audit committees and supervisors can use the framework to tier decision rights by monetary exposure and reversibility, and to require evidence that oversight can actually stop and correct an agent’s actions. Keywords: agentic AI; corporate finance function; financial accountability; managerial oversight; AI governance; agency theory; management control; dynamic capabilities

title: EXPRESS: Securing Supply Chains: Subsidies, Insurance, and Hybrid Incentives under Costly Verification
summary: The rising frequency of supply-chain disruptions—driven by physical shocks and cyber intrusions—underscores the need for coordinated action between governments and private firms. Firms may underinvest in security because they do not internalize the broader social losses generated by supply-chain disruptions. Public intervention is complicated, however, because firms privately know their baseline network security, choose unobservable preventive effort, and are subject to costly and imperfect verification. We develop a game-theoretic framework to compare three policy approaches: an ex-ante, audit-based subsidy; an ex-post, inspection-based insurance mechanism; and hybrid mechanisms that combine preventive support with contingent protection. Insurance performs better in lower-security environments, where incidents under shirking remain sufficiently likely for claims inspection and denied coverage to provide credible deterrence. Subsidies perform better in moderate-to-high-security environments, where pre-incident verification remains effective even as disruptions become less frequent. In regions where both instruments are feasible, we use an efficiency index—prevention per unit of agency cost—to identify the preferred mechanism. We then analyze two hybrid designs. Under delayed inspection, the government provides an up-front subsidy but conditions coverage on post-incident verification. Under early audit, the government verifies compliance before activating both subsidy and coverage. These hybrids can outperform pure mechanisms when effective verification friction is high or when firms face a large investment-benefit gap. The results provide three policy implications. First, governments should segment firms by baseline network security rather than apply a uniform program. Second, improving verification accuracy can be as important as reducing its direct cost. Third, hybrid mechanisms are most appropriate when their stronger incentives justify the additional administrative and compliance burden of layered verification.

title: Design Schools Through Design Theory
summary: Technological progress and the mismatch between education and labor-market needs have led to an oversupply of courses and a reassessment of quality criteria. Drawing on the contemporary predominance of imagery and the digital transformation of design practice, this article examines the evolution of Visual Communication and Graphic Design programs at three internationally recognized institutions: the Glasgow School of Art, Parsons School of Design, and Pratt Institute. The purpose is to analyze the evolution of User Experience (UX) during the digital shift that occurred in Graphic Design and Visual Communication, comparing, precisely, that same UX applied to their schools’ curricula before and after digitalization. The study analyzes this evolution through the theoretical framework of Donald Norman’s concept of “reflective value” across two research dimensions: narrative and context, and interaction and participation. From this perspective, educational programs are understood as designed experiences whose quality depends not only on their curricular content but also on the relationships that they establish between students, educators, and institutions. Through UX theory, it is possible to achieve a more accurate conclusion about design and teaching adaptation in the context of digitalization, and the achievements of all the agents involved: students, educators, and institutions.

title: On specific features of modern information exchange technologies in underground ore mining
summary: Interaction of autonomous equipment in underground ore mining is based on information exchange technologies with a number of specific features and components to ensure the efficiency, safety and sustainability of their operation. The following areas of digital transformation stand out in the medium-term prospective: (1) remote control of mobile equipment that allows technological operations to be performed from safe zones, which is especially important when mining in hazardous areas and areas with increased water content; (2) wireless communication systems in underground conditions in order to implement the project of automated control systems for mobile drilling units; (3) artificial intelligence (digital assistants) for optimizing technological processes, predicting emergency situations, reduction of equipment downtime; (4) creation of “digital twins” of underground mines. In the long term, there are plans to implement the Smart Mine concept, which envisages maximum automation of the production processes with minimal presence of production personnel in the hazardous areas. This article describes operational characteristics of the cyber-physical systems. It presents a diagram of a system for smart connectivity and integration of information and communication technologies into mining machinery as part of robotization of mining systems, which consists of a three-tier top-to-bottom interaction architecture.

title: Digital Leadership, Digital Competence, Work Motivation, Digital Culture, and Employee Performance in Indonesian Local Government: Self-Efficacy as a Mediating Variable
summary: Background: Digital transformation in local government obliges employees to adjust to continually evolving information systems. At the Regional Secretariat of Tangerang Regency, the rollout of the Regional Government Information System (SIPD) sets the context for examining the organizational and psychological factors linked to employee performance. Objective: This study investigates how Digital Leadership affects Employee Performance via the mediating role of Self-Efficacy, while also testing the direct effects of Digital Competence, Work Motivation, and Digital Culture on Employee Performance. Methods: A quantitative approach combining descriptive and verificative methods was used, with primary data obtained from an online questionnaire administered to all 206 employees of the Regional Secretariat of Tangerang Regency through a saturated sampling technique. The data were analyzed with Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results: The reported PLS-SEM estimates indicate positive relationships between the four predictors and Employee Performance, together with a positive indirect relationship between Digital Leadership and Employee Performance through Self-Efficacy. The coefficient for Digital Competence is very small (β = 0.004). Interpretation stays cautious, since the measurement and structural results contain reporting inconsistencies. Conclusion: The findings imply that digital leadership and employee self-efficacy matter for performance in this setting. The cross-sectional design and the limitations in the reported model diagnostics constrain any causal interpretation.

title: TIJORAT BANKLARI FAOLIYATINI TRANSFORMATSIYALASHUV JARAYONINI TAKOMILLASHTIRISH
summary: Annotatsiya. Maqolada O‘zbekiston tijorat banklari faoliyatini transformatsiyalashuv jarayonining nazariy-uslubiy asoslari va amaliy holati tadqiq etilgan. 2020–2025 yillarga mo‘ljallangan bank tizimini isloh qilish strategiyasi doirasida amalga oshirilgan o‘zgarishlar – davlat ulushini qisqartirish, raqobat muhitini kuchaytirish, raqamli bank xizmatlarini rivojlantirish va prudensial barqarorlikni mustahkamlash yo‘nalishlari O‘zbekiston Respublikasi Markaziy banki, Jahon banki va Xalqaro valyuta jamg‘armasi ma’lumotlari asosida baholangan. Tahlil natijalariga ko‘ra, 2021 yil 1 yanvardan 2026 yil 1 yanvargacha bo‘lgan davrda bank tizimi aktivlari 366,1 trln so‘mdan 925,0 trln so‘mgacha o‘sib, o‘rtacha yillik o‘sish sur’ati 20,4 foizni tashkil etgan, masofaviy bank xizmatlaridan foydalanuvchilar soni esa 82,9 mln nafarga yetgan. Shu bilan birga, davlat ulushiga ega banklarning jami aktivlardagi hissasi 63,5 foiz darajasida saqlanib qolayotgani strategiyada belgilangan mo‘ljalga to‘liq erishilmaganini ko‘rsatadi. Tadqiqot natijasida bank transformatsiyasi darajasini baholashning integral indeksi taklif etilgan hamda transformatsiya jarayonini takomillashtirish bo‘yicha ilmiy-amaliy takliflar ishlab chiqilgan. Kalit so‘zlar: tijorat banklari, bank transformatsiyasi, raqamli transformatsiya, xususiylashtirish, raqobat muhiti, konsentratsiya, masofaviy bank xizmatlari, prudensial barqarorlik, Bazel III, fintex. Abstract. The article examines the theoretical, methodological and practical aspects of the transformation of commercial banks in Uzbekistan. Changes implemented under the Banking System Reform Strategy for 2020–2025 – reducing the state share, strengthening competition, developing digital banking services and reinforcing prudential resilience – are assessed using data from the Central Bank of the Republic of Uzbekistan, the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund. Between 1 January 2021 and 1 January 2026, total banking assets grew from UZS 366.1 trillion to UZS 925.0 trillion, a compound annual growth rate of 20.4 percent, while the number of remote banking users reached 82.9 million. At the same time, the share of state-owned banks in total assets remains at 63.5 percent, indicating that the strategic target has not yet been fully achieved. The study proposes an integral index for assessing the level of bank transformation and develops practical recommendations for improving the transformation process. Keywords: commercial banks, bank transformation, digital transformation, privatization, competition, concentration, remote banking services, prudential resilience, Basel III, fintech. Аннотация. В статье исследованы теоретико-методологические основы и современное состояние процесса трансформации деятельности коммерческих банков Узбекистана. В рамках Стратегии реформирования банковской системы Республики Узбекистан на 2020–2025 годы на основе данных Центрального банка Республики Узбекистан, Всемирного банка и Международного валютного фонда проведена оценка изменений, осуществлённых по таким направлениям, как сокращение доли государственного участия, усиление конкурентной среды, развитие цифровых банковских услуг и укрепление пруденциальной устойчивости. По результатам анализа установлено, что за период с 1 января 2021 года по 1 января 2026 года совокупные активы банковской системы увеличились с 366,1 трлн сумов до 925,0 трлн сумов, при этом среднегодовой темп роста составил 20,4 процента, а количество пользователей дистанционных банковских услуг достигло 82,9 млн. Вместе с тем сохранение доли банков с государственным участием в совокупных активах банковской системы на уровне 63,5 процента свидетельствует о неполном достижении целевых показателей, предусмотренных стратегией. В результате исследования предложен интегральный индекс оценки уровня трансформации банков, а также разработаны научно-практические рекомендации по совершенствованию процесса трансформации банковской деятельности. title: Identifying Companies’ Internal Control Deficiency Risks: Evidence from Regulatory Inquiry Letters and Machine Learning
summary: Internal control deficiencies remain a pervasive challenge for listed firms, significantly undermining the stability and growth of capital markets. Although regulatory inquiry letters (RILs) are widely recognized as a critical tool for non-financial information disclosure, their proactive efficacy in identifying and mitigating internal control deficiency risks (ICDR) remains underexplored. This study examines whether RILs can effectively identify latent ICDR and reduce their recurrence in subsequent periods. Using a sample of Chinese listed companies from 2015 to 2022, we employ optimized machine learning algorithms to quantify ICDR as continuous probability values. The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) framework is further applied to rank the relative importance of risk factors and interpret the model’s predictive mechanisms. Our findings demonstrate that the XGBoost model outperforms alternative machine learning algorithms in predicting ICDR, achieving optimal balance between precision and recall. Empirical evidence confirms that RILs not only serve as an effective mechanism for identifying ICDR in advance but also exert a substantive supervisory effect, reducing the likelihood of future deficiencies. These results offer novel insights for the early detection of internal control deficiencies, providing actionable implications for managers, regulators, and investors in evaluating corporate operational performance and mitigating systemic risks.

title: Artificial intelligence promotes urban green innovation in China with regional spillovers and asymmetric climate-risk thresholds
summary: We systematically examine the impact of artificial intelligence on urban green innovation in the context of climate risk. The results demonstrate that artificial intelligence substantially promotes green innovation, an effect primarily transmitted through expanded openness to trade and enhanced scientific-research investment, with the digital economy playing a positive moderating role. Spatial analysis reveals that artificial intelligence advances in one city generate significant positive spillovers that enhance the green innovation performance of neighboring cities. This spatial pattern exhibits pronounced regional heterogeneity: the western region displays significantly positive indirect effects, whereas the eastern and central regions are dominated by direct effects. Threshold effect analysis uncovers differentiated responses to physical climate risks: artificial intelligence’s benefits are weakened once extreme high-temperature days exceed the threshold but strengthened once extreme low-temperature days exceed their threshold, while extreme precipitation exerts no discernible threshold influence. Finally, higher transition risk is found to amplify the beneficial impact of artificial intelligence on green innovation.

title: CULTURAL HERITAGE AND TOURISM DEVELOPMENT IN UZBEKISTAN: SAMARKAND AND BUKHARA
summary: This article examines the role of cultural heritage in the development of tourism in Uzbekistan, focusing on the historical cities of Samarkand and Bukhara. These cities represent important centers of historical, architectural, religious, and cultural heritage and play a significant role in strengthening Uzbekistan's position in the international tourism market. The study analyzes the relationship between cultural heritage preservation and tourism development, with particular attention to economic growth, employment generation, local entrepreneurship, and the preservation of national identity. A qualitative research approach is employed through the analysis of academic literature, international conventions, UNESCO documentation, and official materials. Comparative analysis is used to identify the similarities and differences between Samarkand and Bukhara in terms of historical resources, architectural characteristics, tourism opportunities, and heritage management challenges. The findings indicate that cultural heritage tourism contributes to regional economic development, investment attraction, the expansion of tourism services, and the preservation of traditional cultural practices. However, tourism development also creates challenges related to the conservation of historical monuments, excessive visitor flows, infrastructure management, and the commercialization of cultural values. The article emphasizes the importance of sustainable tourism planning, digital transformation, effective heritage management, and active community participation. It concludes that integrating cultural heritage preservation with tourism development can strengthen the competitiveness of Uzbekistan's tourism sector and support the long-term socioeconomic development of historical cities.

title: Independent in Law, Dependent in Practice: Examining the Effectiveness of Independent Directors under Indian Corporate Governance Law
summary: India's law requires designated independent directors to satisfy detailed eligibility conditions, disclose conflicts, undertake specified duties and sit on committees that supervise financial reporting and appointments. The assumption behind these rules is that a director who lacks disqualifying ties will be able to judge management proposals without undue influence. That assumption is incomplete. A person may comply with every statutory condition yet depend on promoters or an incumbent board for nomination, access to information, committee assignments and a second term. This article examines that dependence through the Companies Act, 2013, the SEBI listing regulations, regulatory reform papers and selected disputes. It argues that the appointment process deserves closer scrutiny than the usual catalogue of independence tests. The law now offers important counterweights, including special-resolution approval and a limited alternative involving public-shareholder support; neither makes the process wholly independent of concentrated ownership. Satyam and IL&FS show what oversight systems are asked to do when management information is unreliable, but do not prove that every independent director in those companies was culpable. A comparison with the United Kingdom and United States suggests reforms centred on nominations, independent information channels, dissent records and evidence-based accountability. The proposed standard measures independence by the director's freedom to question, investigate and, when necessary, oppose the people who secured the appointment.

title: Evolution of Multicriteria Decision Making Methods: A Thirty-Year Review of Theory, Applications, and Future Trends
summary: A bibliometric analysis of multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) studies was conducted using 8,947 articles published between 1995 and 2025. Only studies indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection (SCI-Expanded and SSCI) were considered. An adapted PRISMA protocol and bibliometric methods were applied using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny. The analyses include descriptive statistics, life-cycle modelling, co-citation and bibliographic coupling, keyword co-occurrence, thematic mapping, collaboration networks, and citation structure. The results reveal three growth phases, with acceleration after 2016 and a compound annual growth rate of 21.82% over 1995–2025 (7.4% over 2020–2025). A logistic model fits the trend well (R² = 0.991), indicating 90% of estimated saturation around 2032 (95% bootstrap interval: 2031–2034) if the post-2022 slowdown continues. This estimate is treated as a scenario rather than a forecast. The field's intellectual framework is based on fuzzy set theory and MCDM methods, particularly TOPSIS, AHP, and VIKOR, while its conceptual space has diversified toward sustainability, artificial intelligence, and engineering applications. Collaboration and citation networks reveal a globally distributed but fragmented community, with contributions from China, Türkiye, India, and Iran, and institutional centers in Eastern Europe and Asia. Productivity, citation impact, and collaboration centrality are moderately correlated, indicating that prolific contributors are not necessarily the most cited or central. Web of Science categories confirm the field's interdisciplinary position across environmental sciences, computer science, and operations research. Research gaps include the dominance of five classical methods (92.6% of articles), limited research on rank reversal (1.1%), weak integration of healthcare and agri-food applications into their home disciplines, insufficient attention to digital transformation and the circular economy, and geographical concentration, with four countries producing 55.5% of corresponding-author output. These findings provide a data-driven overview of the field's development, current state, and future directions.

title: A blockchain-enabled U.S. sovereign wealth fund: funding constraints, regulatory barriers, and portfolio implications
summary: The creation of a U.S. sovereign wealth fund (SWF) has long been hindered by fiscal fragmentation, political resistance, and regulatory ambiguity. At the same time, blockchain technology is redefining institutional transparency, asset tokenization, and capital allocation in global finance. This study presents the first empirical simulation of a blockchain-enabled U.S. SWF, evaluating how tokenized asset allocations and on-chain disclosure mechanisms impact risk-adjusted returns and the cost of capital under varying regimes of regulatory and geopolitical uncertainty. Framing the SWF as a politically contingent institutional investor, we assess how financial technologies interact with the U.S. political economy to either amplify or dampen sovereign investment efficiency. Using System-GMM, rolling regressions, and quantile and threshold models across macro-financial data from 2015-2024, we find that Ethereum consistently enhances portfolio performance, but its benefits are highly sensitive to regulatory clarity. In contrast, Bitcoin's volatility renders it unsuitable for sovereign use. These findings underscore how institutional investment outcomes are co-determined by technological design and policy stability, offering new insights into the political economy of sovereign asset governance. Our results speak directly to policymakers, regulators, and institutional investors designing sovereign financial institutions in an era of digital disruption and regulatory flux.

title: The evolution of legitimacy discourse in corporate social responsibility reporting: evidence from a state-owned Irish energy company (2003-2025)
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how legitimacy is discursively constructed and stabilised over time in corporate social responsibility (CSR) reporting in a state-owned enterprise (SOE) and what these legitimacy dynamics reveal about how an SOE responds to evolving sustainable-development expectations. Design/methodology/approach The CSR sections of the Electricity Supply Board’s annual reports from 2003 to 2025 are analysed using a theory-informed computerised content analysis based on Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count categories mapped to Suchman’s (1995) legitimacy framework. To assess the mapping’s interpretive validity, the authors incorporate several robustness analyses. Findings Over the 23-year period studied, the reports increasingly and consistently used language that conveyed a sense of the ESB as a natural, accepted part of everyday life. While the report language reflected pragmatic and moral legitimacy, cognitive legitimacy was prominent. This prominence is observed across multiple analytical approaches, suggesting a stable discursive orientation. This finding suggests that in SOE contexts, legitimacy depends less on actively persuading stakeholders and more on being perceived as taken-for-granted in society. Sustainable-development transitions occur through organisations whose historically embedded societal roles can both support continuity and require continuing accountability as sustainable-development expectations change. Research limitations/implications The study focuses on a single case. Also, the operationalisation of legitimacy through linguistic proxies involves interpretive judgement. While robustness checks provide support for the findings, the results should be understood as indicative patterns, not precise measurements. Practical implications The findings highlight CSR reporting as a component of managing long-term legitimacy, particularly for publicly accountable organisations. Managers may draw on historically embedded narratives and societal connections to enhance trust and alignment with sustainable-development expectations. Social implications For policymakers and regulators, the findings suggest that sustainability reporting is more than a compliance exercise – it is part of a wider infrastructure supporting public accountability and long-term societal value, and this should inform how reporting is designed. For organisations, actively cultivating a sense of being a trusted part of society through reporting can strengthen stakeholder ties and support broader sustainable development efforts. Originality/value This study provides longitudinal evidence on the configuration of legitimacy forms in CSR reporting, showing that legitimacy dynamics in SOEs differ from prior literature and the relevance of historically accumulated legitimacy to sustainable development. It also contributes methodologically by proxying legitimacy types to automated text analysis.
